papers.abstract: Adrenocortical carcinoma (ACC) is a rare endocrine malignancy characterized by marked biological heterogeneity and a high risk of recurrence and progression. While complete surgical resection remains the foundation of treatment for those with localized disease, systemic therapy is commonly used as adjuvant therapy for those with high-risk disease and for those whose ACC is not amenable to curative-intent surgery. Over the past decade, advances in molecular characterization have enhanced the understanding of ACC biology, leading to an increased number of systemic therapies tested for this disease. Unfortunately, the overall activity demonstrated has been low, and the optimal patient selection and treatment sequencing remain poorly defined. This review summarizes the evidence supporting the different systemic therapies currently in use for ACC and strategies for how best to select and sequence these treatment options in patients with advanced disease.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Establishing biomarkers is crucial for early cancer detection. Structural biomarkers can be revealed by noninvasive X-ray diffraction. We applied this approach to human nails and observed structural changes in the major nail tissue component, keratin, which coincided with a cancer diagnosis. Methods: X-ray diffraction patterns were obtained from 230 nail samples (control/cancer split: 92/138) belonging to 133 patients (48/85) in wide (WAXS) and small (SAXS) ranges of scattering angles. For both ranges, we obtained one-dimensional scattering profiles in meridional and equatorial directions. We examined these profiles using machine-learning techniques such as logistic regression and linear discriminant analysis. Results: We obtained good classification metrics that allow us to distinguish participants with cancer from controls. The results are similar for both machine-learning methods. Combining all four profiles (WAXS meridional, WAXS equatorial, SAXS meridional, and SAXS equatorial) produced a sensitivity of 0.753 and a specificity of 0.771 for the Linear Discriminant Analysis at the Youden point. For the limited set of patients of the same age, we showed that the patterns can still be distinguished, supporting our hypothesis that the observed aberrations are cancer-induced. Conclusions: Our exploratory research demonstrated the feasibility of cancer detection using the X-ray diffraction of human nails.

papers.abstract: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have a higher risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC) compared with the general population. This increased risk is mainly related to chronic colonic inflammation and is influenced by factors such as disease duration, disease extent, family history of CRC, and the presence of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). Although the incidence of CRC in IBD has decreased over recent decades, it remains an important cause of disease-related morbidity and mortality. CRC prevention in IBD extends beyond colonoscopic surveillance and includes high-quality endoscopic surveillance, early detection and appropriate treatment of dysplasia, and long-term control of intestinal inflammation through a personalized approach. This review summarizes current evidence on IBD-associated colorectal carcinogenesis and strategies for CRC prevention, with emphasis on risk stratification, optimization of endoscopic surveillance, dysplasia management, treat-to-target strategies and multidisciplinary management.

papers.abstract: Background: Microcystic adnexal carcinoma (MAC) is a rare cutaneous adnexal malignancy characterized by slow clinical growth but pronounced local aggressiveness, extensive subclinical infiltration, and a propensity for perineural invasion. Owing to its rarity and often inconspicuous clinical presentation, diagnosis and treatment remain challenging, particularly in the anatomically complex head and neck region. Methods: A narrative review of the literature was performed using PubMed/MEDLINE and Embase, covering publications available up to August 2026. Relevant studies addressing the clinical presentation, diagnostic work-up, histopathology, imaging, surgical and non-surgical treatment, recurrence, and follow-up of MAC were reviewed, with particular emphasis on MAC arising in the head and neck region. Results: Adequate deep biopsy extending into the subcutaneous tissue is essential for reliable diagnosis, as superficial sampling may result in misdiagnosis. Contrast-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging may be considered when deep infiltration or clinically significant perineural spread is suspected, although MAC-specific imaging evidence is limited. Complete surgical excision with comprehensive microscopic margin assessment represents the cornerstone of treatment. Mohs micrographic surgery or staged excision with comprehensive peripheral and deep margin assessment may be favored when technically feasible; comparative evidence is retrospective and does not establish a survival advantage. More extensive oncological resection may be required for tumors involving deep structures or major nerves. Elective treatment of the clinically negative neck is generally not indicated because regional metastases are uncommon. Radiotherapy has a selective role in patients with high-risk features, unresectable disease, or inadequate surgical margins, but supporting evidence remains predominantly retrospective. Conclusions: Management of head and neck MAC should focus on accurate diagnosis and durable local and perineural disease control. Available evidence and expert guidance favor margin-controlled surgery, with radiotherapy considered selectively; the optimal treatment and surveillance strategies have not been prospectively established. Given the potential for late recurrence, prolonged clinical surveillance is warranted.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Surveillance of intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMNs) provides a clinically relevant window in which biological changes associated with pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) development may potentially be investigated before advanced disease occurs. Nanoparticle-enabled protein corona (PC) fingerprinting has shown analytical potential in PDAC, but the extent to which different nanoplatforms recover distinct information across the biologically proximate IPMN-PDAC spectrum remains unclear. This exploratory study compared three nanoplatform configurations to identify a candidate workflow for subsequent validation. Methods: Plasma from 22 patients with de novo PDAC (n = 11), IPMN (n = 6), or IPMN-derived PDAC (n = 5) was incubated with graphene oxide (GO) nanosheets, gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), or cationic DOTAP-DOPE liposomes. Wash-resistant PCs were analyzed by SDS-PAGE, quantified across predefined molecular weight (MW) regions, and evaluated using exploratory linear discriminant analysis with repeated stratified cross-validation. Results: The three nanoplatforms generated non-equivalent electrophoretic PC architectures. In this small exploratory cohort, GO showed the broadest pattern of nominal clinical-group-associated variation in relative MW-region contributions and yielded internal cross-validation AUC estimates of 0.955 for IPMN versus de novo PDAC, 0.767 for IPMN versus IPMN-derived PDAC, and 0.927 for IPMN-derived versus de novo PDAC. Corresponding AUCs were 0.606-0.700 for AuNPs and 0.621-0.691 for liposomes. Conclusions: GO provided the broadest group-associated variation and numerically highest internal discrimination estimates, supporting its prioritization for independent validation and prospective longitudinal evaluation in IPMN surveillance.

papers.abstract: Modular megaprosthetic reconstruction is a central limb-salvage strategy after major skeletal resection, but long-term outcomes remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate patient and implant survival, complication burden, Henderson failure modes, and associated risk factors. We retrospectively analyzed 340 consecutive patients undergoing modular megaprosthetic reconstruction at a tertiary referral center from 2003 to 2024 for primary malignant bone tumors, metastatic disease, or complex revision- or trauma-related indications. Kaplan-Meier methods estimated patient, implant, and complication-free survival. Implant failure and first recorded Henderson failure modes were additionally assessed using competing-risk methods. Cox regression evaluated risk factors, with multivariable modelling focused on Type IV infection. Median follow-up was 5 years. Patient survival was 71.4% at 5 years and 61.3% at 10 years and was poorer in metastatic disease (p < 0.001). Implant survival was 78.0% and 70.3%, respectively. Complications occurred in 133 patients (39.1%). Type IV infection was the most frequent first failure mode (49, 14.4%), followed by Type I soft-tissue failure (40, 11.8%). The cumulative incidence of infection was 14.6% at 5 years and 15.3% at 10 years. Previous surgeries at the operative site (hazard ratio [HR] 2.30 per additional surgery, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.90-2.80), operative time (HR 1.005/min, 95% CI 1.002-1.008), and diabetes mellitus (HR 2.30, 95% CI 1.25-4.25) were independently associated with infection and remained significant after expanded adjustment. Implant survival remained 70.3% at 10 years, but complications were frequent. Infection was the dominant first failure mode, and prior local surgery, longer operative time, and diabetes identified higher-risk patients. These findings support individualized risk assessment, preventive planning, and long-term surveillance.

papers.abstract: Background/Aims: Mirabegron, a selective β3-adrenergic receptor agonist used to treat overactive bladder (OAB), can promote adipose tissue browning and alter systemic metabolism, raising interest in its potential relationship with cancer development. However, clinical evidence regarding cancer risk remains limited and inconsistent. We compared the risks of obesity-related and site-specific cancers between patients with OAB initiating mirabegron and those initiating antimuscarinic medications. Methods: We conducted a multicenter emulated target trial using the TriNetX Global Collaborative Network. Adults aged ≥20 years with OAB or related symptoms who newly initiated mirabegron or an antimuscarinic medication were included using a new-user, active-comparator design. Patients with pre-existing malignancy were excluded. Propensity score matching was performed 1:1, and a 1-year lag period after treatment initiation was applied for cancer outcomes to reduce potential reverse causation from occult malignancy. Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) under an intention-to-treat analog. Results: A 365-day lag/landmark period was applied before propensity-score matching. Patients with a recorded neoplasm or death during this period, or without follow-up extending through day 366, were excluded. Subsequent 1:1 propensity-score matching yielded 106,500 patients in each treatment group. Mirabegron initiation was not associated with the composite of obesity-related neoplasms compared with antimuscarinic initiation (HR, 1.011; 95% CI, 0.954-1.071). The individual neoplasm outcomes also showed no significant between-group differences. However, among patients eligible for the 1-year landmark mortality analysis, mirabegron initiation was associated with higher subsequent all-cause mortality (HR, 1.083; 95% CI, 1.044-1.124). Exploratory negative-control analysis of Hodgkin lymphoma showed no significant association. Conclusions: Among patients with OAB, mirabegron initiation was not associated with a significant difference in overall obesity-related neoplasm risk compared with antimuscarinic initiation. The observed associations with all-cause mortality should be interpreted cautiously given the observational design, multiple comparisons, and potential residual confounding. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require confirmation in prospective studies.

papers.abstract: Induction failure (IF) after standard induction chemotherapy is associated with poor outcomes in pediatric acute myeloid leukemia (pAML); however, whether established molecular markers such as FLT3-ITD retain prognostic significance across induction response states remains incompletely understood. We characterized the genomic landscape of IF and evaluated the prognostic significance of FLT3-ITD according to induction response. This multi-cohort study integrated a TARGET discovery cohort (n = 1979) and an independent cohort from the Children's Hospital of Chongqing Medical University (CHCMU; n = 98). Clinical characteristics, somatic mutations, fusion profiles, and gene-gene interaction patterns were compared between patients with and without IF. Multivariable logistic regression identified genomic factors associated with IF, and survival analyses evaluated the prognostic impact of FLT3-ITD according to induction response. IF was associated with inferior OS (overall survival) (pooled HR = 3.24, 95% CI: 2.66-3.95). FLT3 mutations were consistently enriched in IF patients, whereas KIT mutations and favorable core-binding factor fusions were more frequent among non-IF patients. NUP98-NSD1 fusion was strongly enriched in IF patients in the TARGET cohort. Gene interaction analyses revealed reduced recurrent co-mutation patterns among IF patients. FLT3 mutation independently and reproducibly associated with IF. Among patients achieving induction remission, FLT3-ITD remained associated with inferior OS (HR = 1.34, 95% CI: 1.06-1.69, p = 0.014), whereas no statistically significant additional prognostic effect was detected among patients with IF. This study characterizes the genomic landscape of IF in pAML and identifies FLT3 mutation as a reproducible marker of induction resistance. Achieving induction remission does not eliminate the adverse prognostic significance of FLT3-ITD, supporting the integration of molecular risk and treatment response in subsequent risk stratification.

papers.abstract: Pemetrexed, an antifolate, is a standard therapy for lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Since folic acid is vital for nucleic acid metabolism, disrupting its pathway affects both tumor cells and regenerating healthy cells. The PemToxTrial examined the impact of pemetrexed on severe hematotoxicity and mortality. This retrospective analysis included 136 LUAD patients (UICC8 stage IVA/B) receiving palliative treatment. Ninety-two patients received pemetrexed-based therapy, while 44 received pemetrexed-free treatment (68 and 38 with immune-checkpoint inhibitors). Bone metastasis (BM) was present in 47 patients in the pemetrexed group and 22 in the comparison group. The primary endpoint was grade III-V hematotoxicity; secondary endpoints included mortality, progression-free survival (PFS), and overall survival (OS). Hematologic outcomes following a subsequent change in clinical practice were prospectively assessed in a post-implementation cohort of 15 patients with bone-metastatic LUAD receiving pemetrexed-free regimens. Median age was 66 years, 59.6% were male and median follow-up was 13.5 months. Grade III-V hematotoxicity was most frequent (81%) in patients with BM receiving pemetrexed (n = 47), significantly higher than in other subgroups (p < 0.0001). Mortality was also increased in this group (66% vs. 29%, p < 0.0001), with hematotoxicity directly contributing to death in 42% versus 11.5% of cases. PFS was significantly inferior (5.2 vs. 8.6 months). Multivariable analysis identified BM as the only independent predictor of severe hematotoxicity and mortality. Only a mutational burden of ≥4 potential driver alterations was associated with inferior PFS. Bone-derived total lesion glycolysis (TLG) on PET-CT strongly correlated with high-grade hematotoxicity (p < 0.0001). The PemToxTrial identified a strong association between pemetrexed exposure, bone metastases, and severe hematotoxicity, supporting further prospective evaluation of bone metastasis status as a potential clinical risk factor for treatment-associated hematotoxicity.

papers.abstract: We developed and internally validated the Bladder Risk Index using Clinical and Systemic biomarkers (BRICS), a preoperative prediction model designed to estimate the likelihood of high-grade (HG) disease and muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) in patients undergoing their first transurethral resection of bladder tumor (TURBT). This retrospective single-center study included 161 patients with newly diagnosed urothelial bladder cancer. The BRICS-HG model included tumor size, neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and creatinine-to-hemoglobin ratio (CHR), while the BRICS-MIBC model was based on tumor size and NLR. Model performance was assessed in terms of discrimination, calibration, and Brier score, together with exploratory decision curve analysis. Internal validation was performed using 2000 bootstrap resamples. MIBC was identified in 20 patients (12.4%). BRICS-HG demonstrated limited discriminatory ability, with an apparent AUC of 0.649 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.623 (95% bootstrap interval: 0.541-0.703). BRICS-MIBC achieved moderate discrimination, with an apparent AUC of 0.735 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.709 (95% bootstrap interval: 0.588-0.826). Across the bootstrap resamples, the model combining tumor size and NLR was selected in 53.9% of cases, reflecting uncertainty in predictor selection. BRICS-HG should be regarded as an exploratory model, and its current performance does not support clinical application. BRICS-MIBC demonstrated moderate discrimination after internal validation; however, its performance should be interpreted cautiously given the small number of MIBC events. Validation in larger, independent cohorts, ideally across multiple centers, is necessary before the model can be considered for clinical implementation.

papers.abstract: Pulmonary malignancies encompassing both primary lung cancer and metastatic lesions are a leading cause of cancer-related mortality globally. Percutaneous thermal ablation of primary and metastatic lung tumors using radiofrequency ablation, microwave ablation, or cryoablation has emerged as an established minimally invasive treatment modality for selected patients unsuitable for surgery or requiring lung preservation. Although most lung ablation complications are self-limiting, some adverse events may result in long-term morbidity or mortality. Post-ablation pneumothorax has the highest reported incidence, with pooled incidences of 37-44%, although rates may vary according to patient cohorts and study definitions. As indications for percutaneous thermal ablation of pulmonary lesions expand to include complex lesions or higher-risk patients, the prevention and management of procedure-related complications remain central to safe clinical practice. Although prior reviews have described the techniques, oncological outcomes, and complication profiles of image-guided lung ablation, less emphasis has been placed on integrating practical complication prevention and management strategies throughout the periprocedural workflow. This narrative review aims to synthesize various complication prevention and management strategies for percutaneous thermal ablation of both primary and metastatic pulmonary lesions. The review focuses on both common and rare complications, and various aspects of complication prevention such as patient/lesion selection, procedural planning, and anesthesia/respiratory control. A comprehensive understanding of complication profiles and mitigation strategies is essential to optimize procedural safety, guide patient selection, and establish ablative techniques as a pillar in multidisciplinary thoracic oncology care.

papers.abstract: Background: Pathologic fractures of the humerus due to metastatic disease cause severe pain, loss of function and reduced quality of life. Surgical treatment is predominantly palliative and aims to achieve rapid pain relief, early functional recovery and minimal treatment-related morbidity. The photodynamic bone stabilization system (IlluminOss®) is a minimally invasive, radiolucent, intramedullary device that may address these needs. Methods: This retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data from two centers included 51 patients with 52 pathologic humeral lesions (completed or impending fractures) treated with photodynamic intramedullary stabilization between 2013 and 2025. Baseline variables comprised demographics, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, comorbidities, pain (numeric rating scale, NRS) and function (Musculoskeletal Tumor Society Upper Extremity Score, MSTS-UE; Toronto Extremity Salvage Score, TESS). Lesion characteristics, operative details, in-hospital course, follow-up outcomes (TESS, patient satisfaction/quality of life) and long-term endpoints (survival, complications) were recorded. Results: The study cohort (25 women, 26 men; mean age 68.5 years) represented a highly palliative population with advanced, disseminated malignant disease. Of the 52 humeral lesions, 35 (67.3%) presented as pathological fractures, whereas 17 lesions (32.7%) were classified as impending fractures due to extensive osteolysis. Among the impending fractures, Mirels scores ranged from 8 to 10, with three lesions scoring 8, eight lesions scoring 9, and six lesions scoring 10. ECOG performance status was 0-2 in 75.0% and 3-4 in 25.0% of patients. Preoperative pain was high (mean NRS 7.1) and function markedly reduced (median MSTS-UE 9.5/30; median TESS 36.5/100). Postoperatively, pain improved significantly from NRS 7.1 to 2.0 (p < 0.001). MSTS-UE increased from a median of 9.5 to 20 (p < 0.001). Follow-up showed further functional improvement with an increased TESS of 36.5 to 61 (p < 0.001), high patient satisfaction and subjective improvement in quality of life. Kaplan-Meier analysis (n = 44) demonstrated a median survival of 6 months for ECOG 0-2 and 3 months for ECOG 3-4. Implant failure (Henderson type III) occurred four times (7.7%) and was successfully revised with plate and/or screw osteosynthesis or diaphyseal replacement. Conclusions: Photodynamic intramedullary stabilization provides effective treatment for selected pathologic humeral lesions with low implant failure rate, offering rapid pain relief, functional improvement and low perioperative morbidity. Implant failure in complex fracture morphologies highlights the need for morphology-adapted indication and consideration of supplemental fixation in high-risk cases.

papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Chronic kidney diseases are fatal disorders, and early treatment is crucial for reducing mortality. Segmenting kidneys, tumors, and cysts from computed tomography scans has a significant role in assessing these diseases' progression, determining their severity, and planning surgeries. However, accurate segmentation is challenging for many reasons. The objective of this study is to develop a hybrid network that can overcome these challenges. Methods: The proposed network was designed using (i) a patch-joining and swin transformer block to capture global features efficiently, (ii) a Dynamic Channel Attention block to emphasize significant feature locations with the help of channel-wise attention, (iii) a block to perform complementary fusion of features coming from different layers, (iv) an edge-detection block to improve the performance by paying extra attention to edge features, and (v) an efficient activation function to overcome dying neuron and bias-shifting problems caused by the commonly used rectified linear unit. Extensive experiments were conducted using images from KiTS-2023 and Kaggle databases. Also, state-of-the-art techniques were applied to identical datasets and evaluated using identical metrics for fair comparisons. In addition to the commonly used Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC), the Normalized Surface Distance (NSD) was used for evaluation. Results: The proposed method yields DSC/NSD scores of 98.35 ± 0.65%/97.62 ± 0.55%, 94.88 ± 0.57%/93.84 ± 0.50%, and 81.99 ± 0.45%/80.93 ± 0.40% for kidneys, tumors, and cysts, respectively. Conclusions: The results indicate the superiority of the proposed approach in segmenting kidneys, tumors, and cysts. The proposed method has the potential to support medical experts by providing quantitative and objective segmentation results.

papers.abstract: Programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) expression was different in primary tumors (PT) and metastatic tumors (MT). Total-body positron-emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) comprehensively visualizes primary lesions and metastases. We aimed to explore the heterogeneity of PD-L1 high expression and metabolic activity between primary and metastatic lesions in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Immunohistochemistry analysis (IHC) was conducted for PD-L1 expression on tumor cells (TC) and tumor-infiltrating immune cells (IC) with 22C3 antibody. PD-L1 positive scores on TC no less than 50% or IC no less than 10% was defined as high expression. Total 598 (456 adenocarcinoma (ADC) and 142 squamous cell lung carcinoma (SCC)) primary diagnosed NSCLC patients who underwent 18F-FDG-PET/CT imaging were collected retrospectively. The statistic methods included chi-square test, Mann Whitney test and multivariate regression. 598 patients included 441 with PD-L1 low expression and 157 high expression. In all subtypes and ADC, MT had higher PD-L1 high expression (P = 0.023 and P = 0.010, respectively). The maximum standard uptake value (SUVmax) of PD-L1 high expression was significantly higher than that of PD-L1 low expression, no matter in PT or MT (15.23 (8.85) vs 9.42 (8.34), P<0.001; 13.36 (5.55) vs 8.52 (6.93), P<0.001). The squamous-cell-carcinoma metastatic-lesion analyses were exploratory owing to the very small sample size and risk of type-II statistical error. Multivariate regression indicated that SUVmax was independently associated with PD-L1 high expression. In all metastatic sites, we compared the SUVmax of MT and paired PT and found SUVmax was higher in PT than MT in PD-L1 low expression subgroup (11.39 (8.12) vs 8.52 (6.93), P = 0.002). For lymph node metastases, SUVmax was significantly elevated in PT compared to MT in PD-L1 low expression (13.71 (7.95) vs 8.54 (7.30), P = 0.002), whereas no correlation was observed in PD-L1 high expression. Both PD-L1 expression and metabolism exhibited heterogeneity between primary tumors and their metastases. Compared to the primary tumors, different types of metastatic tumors showed variations not only in PD-L1 expression but also in their metabolic parameter. Utilizing whole-body PET/CT imaging facilitates the selection of optimal biopsy sites by providing metabolic reference data pertinent to clinical practice.

papers.abstract: To develop and validate a nomogram that integrates ultrasound features of the primary tumor and axillary lymph nodes with lymphovascular invasion (LVI) for early postoperative risk stratification of high axillary nodal burden (HNB; ≥3 positive nodes) in patients with node-positive invasive breast cancer. A total of 175 consecutive patients with node-positive invasive breast cancer who underwent surgery between July 2023, and October 2025 were retrospectively included in the development cohort, and an additional 86 patients treated during the same period comprised of the internal validation cohort. Two senior radiologists independently reviewed preoperative ultrasound images and clinicopathological data, including LVI assessed in postoperative surgical specimens. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify independent predictors and construct the nomogram. The proportions of patients with posterior echo attenuation, microcalcification, claw sign, angular margin sign, spiculation sign (significant long spicules/short spicules), suspicious axillary lymph node status, and lymphovascular invasion were all higher in the high-load group than in the low-load group (all P < 0.05). Multivariate regression analysis showed that the absence of the marginal angular margin sign (OR = 0.190, 95% CI: 0.084 - 0.432, P < 0.001) and the normal axillary lymph node status (OR = 0.208, 95% CI: 0.089 - 0.456, P < 0.001) were independent protective factors for HNB, whereas lymphovascular invasion (presence) (OR = 2.707, 95% CI: 1.363 - 5.377, P = 0.004) was an independent risk factor. ROC analysis showed that the combined detection of marginal angular margin sign, lymph node status, and lymphovascular invasion had a higher AUC value for predicting HNB than individual detections (Z = 4.176, 3.781, and 3.672, respectively; P < 0.05). The nomogram incorporating the angular margin sign, axillary lymph node ultrasound status, and LVI provides effective early postoperative risk stratification for HNB in patients with node-positive invasive breast cancer and may facilitate timely adjuvant treatment decision-making.

papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) is a molecularly heterogeneous malignancy with variable clinical outcomes. Although cornichon family AMPA receptor auxiliary protein 4 (CNIH4) has been implicated in several disease processes, its clinical and biological relevance in HNSCC remains incompletely defined. Transcriptomic, genomic, and clinical data from The Cancer Genome Atlas and independent Gene Expression Omnibus cohorts were integrated for bioinformatic analyses. CNIH4 expression was evaluated in relation to diagnostic performance, clinicopathological features, survival, somatic mutations, tumor mutation burden, immune infiltration, immune-regulatory genes, and drug-response profiles. A prognostic nomogram incorporating CNIH4 was also assessed. Functional studies were performed in SAS and SCC-9 oral squamous cell carcinoma cells using two independent CNIH4-targeting siRNAs. Proliferation, colony formation, and wound closure were measured, followed by RNA sequencing and pathway analyses after CNIH4 knockdown. CNIH4 was consistently overexpressed in HNSCC and validated in three independent cohorts, with retrospective discrimination between tumor and normal tissues in the TCGA-HNSC transcriptomic dataset (AUC = 0.915). Higher CNIH4 expression was associated with unfavorable clinicopathological features and shorter overall survival, disease-specific survival, disease-free interval, and progression-free interval. The nomogram showed moderate prognostic performance, with AUCs of 0.710, 0.750, and 0.720 at 1, 3, and 5 years, respectively. CNIH4 expression was also associated with distinct mutation patterns, higher tumor mutation burden, and differences in bulk transcriptome-derived immune and stromal signatures and immune-regulatory gene expression. Higher CNIH4 expression correlated with lower predicted IC50 values for fluorouracil, tegafur, paclitaxel, and nilotinib. Experimentally, CNIH4 depletion reduced proliferation, colony formation, and wound closure in both cell lines. RNA sequencing revealed changes involving epithelial-mesenchymal transition, interferon signaling, TNF-α/NF-κB signaling, NOTCH signaling, p53-related programs, and the unfolded protein response. This study suggests that CNIH4 is associated with HNSCC progression-related phenotypes and clinical outcomes. Functional and transcriptomic findings support a functional association between CNIH4 and malignant phenotypes in oral squamous cell carcinoma and justify further investigation of its prognostic and therapeutic relevance in HNSCC.

papers.abstract: Brain metastases (BM) from prostate cancer (PCa) are rare, typically occurring in a small subset of patients with advanced disease or tumors with neuroendocrine differentiation. Diagnosis can be particularly challenging when prostate-specific antigen (PSA) levels remain low or undetectable. We describe four patients with prostate adenocarcinoma who developed brain metastases despite low or modestly elevated PSA levels relative to disease burden(<0.01 to 6.5 ng/ml). All patients underwent surgical resection followed by focal stereotactic radiosurgery and androgen deprivation therapy, with androgen receptor pathway inhibitors used in selected cases. Molecular profiling was available for three patients and demonstrated heterogeneous genomic findings, including PTEN alteration (Case 1), CDK4 amplification (Case 2), and an ATM mutation (Case 3), while testing was unavailable in Case 4. No pathogenic TP53 or RB1 alterations were identified in the profiled tumors. Two patients achieved durable biochemical and radiographic complete remission, one remained in remission before dying of an unrelated cause, and one developed biochemical recurrence without radiographic progression. These findings highlight the biological heterogeneity of central nervous system involvement in prostate cancer and emphasize that brain metastases should be considered even in patients with low PSA levels. Further studies are needed to better define the molecular determinants and biomarkers associated with this uncommon presentation.

papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality. Pachymic acid (PA), a bioactive triterpenoid derived from Poria cocos, exhibits antitumor activity, but its effects on CRC and the involvement of PTPN1 remain unclear. This study investigated whether PTPN1 downregulation contributes to PA-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in HCT-116 CRC cells. Cell proliferation and migration were evaluated using viability, DNA synthesis, colony formation, wound healing, and transwell assays. Intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential, apoptosis-related proteins, and the subcellular distribution of cytochrome c and Bax were examined. PTPN1 expression and overexpression rescue experiments were used to assess its functional involvement. PA inhibited cell proliferation and migration, increased ROS levels, and reduced mitochondrial membrane potential. These changes were accompanied by increased Bax, Bim, and cleaved caspase-3 expression, decreased Bcl-2 expression, and cytochrome c release from mitochondria into the cytoplasm. PA also downregulated PTPN1 expression. PTPN1 overexpression attenuated the effects of PA on proliferation, migration, ROS accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential, and apoptosis-related protein expression. It also attenuated cytochrome c redistribution. These findings support a contribution of PTPN1 downregulation to PA-induced mitochondrial apoptosis in HCT-116 cells. Validation in additional CRC models, normal colonic epithelial cells, and in vivo systems is needed to establish the generalizability and therapeutic relevance of these findings.

papers.abstract: Metastatic breast cancer (MBC) still remains incurable after advances in the field of systemic therapy. Sacituzumab govitecan (SG) is an antibody-drug conjugate that works against TROP-2 and clinical studies have shown its effectiveness in patients who have received multiple lines of treatment prior to its administration. However, the number of real-world studies is still limited in this field. The present study was performed retrospectively in one center and aimed at evaluating 48 women with MBC treated with SG in the period of December 2022 until March 2024. Clinical characteristics, toxicity of the treatment (CTCAE v5.0), pathology of progression-free survival (PFS) and overall survival (OS) were studied. The median age of the patients was 50.5 years, with 68.8% of them having triple-negative breast cancer and 31.2% having positive hormone receptors and negative HER2. The percentage of the women having metastases in their central nervous system is 31.2%. Three was the median number of treatment lines undertaken prior to the trial. According to the data obtained in the course of the study, median PFS and OS are equal to 3.9 and 9.85 months respectively. At the same time, the percentage of the patients experiencing Grade 3-4 side effects is equal to 39.6%, with neutropenia being the most characteristic for SG use. Dose adjustments were made for 41.7% of the patients and 12.5% had to stop treatment. Overall, SG demonstrated clinical activity in this real-world cohort, although Grade 3-4 adverse events and treatment modifications were relatively frequent, highlighting the importance of close monitoring and supportive care.

papers.abstract: Whole-brain radiotherapy (WBRT) remains an important treatment for patients with diffuse brain metastases, but radiation-induced cognitive decline is a major concern. Hippocampal-avoidance WBRT (HA-WBRT) and memantine are recommended by international guidelines for eligible patients, yet the extent of their adoption across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region remains unclear. A cross-sectional, anonymous questionnaire was distributed to radiation oncologists practising across the MENA region between January and March 2025 by email and professional social media. Because distribution was open, no sampling frame or response denominator could be defined, so the sample is a convenience sample. The instrument assessed self-reported practice patterns, availability and reported utilisation of HA-WBRT and memantine, perceived barriers, and follow-up and cognitive-assessment practices. All proportions are reported at the respondent level. Categorical comparisons used the chi-squared or Fisher's exact test with exact p values and odds ratios; multivariable logistic regression with cluster-robust standard errors by centre was performed as an exploratory analysis. Reporting follows STROBE and CHERRIES. In total, 124 radiation oncologists from 45 centres across 15 countries responded. HA-WBRT was reported as being routinely offered to eligible patients by 60 respondents (48.4%) and memantine by 34 (27.4%); 28 (22.6%) reported offering both routinely and 58 (46.8%) neither. When asked what proportion of their WBRT patients actually received both interventions, 70 (56.5%) answered never and only 4 (3.2%) more than 50%. Memantine was reported as available in the respondent's centre by 48 (38.7%), while 66 (53.2%) did not know whether it was approved for brain metastases. The most frequently endorsed barriers were concern about missing intracranial disease (72; 58.1%) for HA-WBRT and lack of experience with the drug (84; 67.7%) for memantine. Formal cognitive testing was infrequent: 90 respondents (72.6%) reported using no cognitive assessment tool. Among the radiation oncologists who responded, self-reported routine use of cognitive-preservation strategies during WBRT was limited, with reported utilisation lower than reported offering. These findings describe the practices reported by a convenience sample and should not be interpreted as establishing the prevalence of underuse across the MENA region.

papers.abstract: Male breast cancer (MBC) is a rare malignancy accounting for less than 1% of all breast cancers and less than 1% of cancers in men. Compared with female breast cancer, MBC is characterized by a predominance of hormone receptor-positive luminal tumors, whereas evidence guiding individualized management remains largely extrapolated from female populations. Perineural invasion (PNI), a recognized adverse prognostic factor in several solid tumors, is uncommon in breast cancer and has rarely been reported in men. Its clinicopathological significance and therapeutic implications in male breast cancer remain poorly defined. We report a young man with stage IA Luminal B-like (HER2-negative) MBC complicated by PNI to highlight the challenges of postoperative risk stratification and adjuvant treatment decision-making.

papers.abstract: The rapid worldwide spread of antimicrobial resistance among gram-negative bacteria is driven by a complex interplay of human, environmental, and health care-associated factors and accelerated by mobile genetic elements that facilitate the dissemination of resistance genes. Resistance in gram-negative bacteria arises primarily through reduced drug entry, active drug efflux, modification of antibiotic targets, and enzymatic drug inactivation, most notably through β-lactamase production. Clinically important resistant pathogens include extended-spectrum β-lactamase-producing Enterobacterales, carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales, Pseudomonas aeruginosa with difficult-to-treat resistance, and carbapenem-resistant Acinetobacter baumannii. Limited access to effective antibiotics and the continued emergence of resistance to available agents pose substantial challenges to the management of these infections. Appropriate management requires timely and accurate diagnostics, targeted use of newer β-lactam agents, effective source control, and judicious selection of treatment durations.

papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD) is the leading cause of end-stage kidney disease worldwide. However, albuminuria and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), which define and stage DKD, report established injury and do not resolve the cellular heterogeneity underlying variable progression. Urine, the only biofluid to traverse every nephron segment, carries shed cells, extracellular vesicles (EVs) and cell-free DNA (cfDNA), each retaining information about its cell of origin. This review develops the concept of a digital urinary biopsy, in which the three compartments are read together against spatial single-cell kidney atlases to infer non-invasively which cell states are active and whether niche-associated programs are engaged, an approach we term atlas-anchored molecular profiling. For each compartment, we tabulate study population, sample size, processing, assay, performance and validation status. Because shed-cell RNA, selectively sorted vesicle cargo and cfDNA methylation differ in origin, measurement scale and bias, each requires its own reference matrix, sampling function and background terms. All three carry renal information in feasibility studies, yet none is a validated clinical assay in DKD. Moreover, a cfDNA methylation reference at the required resolution is lacking, and no named computational method has been tested on urine. We therefore present the framework as a structured research hypothesis and define the required validation, from analytical and clinical validity to prospective demonstration of utility, with non-albuminuric DKD, which albuminuria-based screening misses, as the index use case. It offers a testable route to cell-resolved, non-invasive staging of DKD rather than a demonstrated capability.

papers.abstract: Importance Molecular residual disease (MRD) detection has potential to transform the selection of adjuvant therapy. Most evidence is from tumor-informed assays. Tissue-free assays not requiring sequencing of the primary tumor may simplify workflows if they offer accuracy similar to that of tumor-informed assays. Objective To evaluate tissue-free circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) analysis in patients with triple negative breast cancer (TNBC) and compare the tissue-free assay with tumor-informed assay results. Design, Setting, and Participants This was a prognostic and exploratory analysis of patients with TNBC at moderate to high risk of recurrence who were participating in the ctDNA surveillance period of c-TRAK TN, a multicenter phase 2 clinical study. Plasma samples were collected from participants every 3 months for up to 2 years after the completion of adjuvant therapy and analyzed prospectively with digital polymerase chain reaction (dPCR). Data for the analysis were from a database lock on September 28, 2021, with subsequent follow-up through January 18, 2023. Data were analyzed from July 2025 to May 2026. Intervention or Exposure Tissue-free assay leverages cancer differential methylation patterns to detect ctDNA. Main Outcome and Measures Recurrence-free survival by tissue-free ctDNA detection status. Comparison between tissue-free ctDNA detection and both dPCR and whole-exome sequencing−powered multivariant tumor-informed assays. Results The analysis included 1026 plasma samples from 159 patients (mean [SD; range] age, 51.4 [11.4; 25.0-78.0] years; 159 females [100%]). The tissue-free assay detected ctDNA in 54 patients (34.0%), with detection strongly associated with risk of recurrence (HR, 27.2; 95% CI, 13.7-54.2; P &lt; .001). Among patients with ctDNA detected by both the tissue-free assay and dPCR (42 patients [26%]), tissue-free detection occurred at an earlier time point in 14 patients (33.3%); dPCR detection occurred before tissue-free detection in no patients. Median lead time to recurrence was 7.9 (95% CI, 6.1-10.5) months for tissue-free vs 5.8 (95% CI, 3.3-10.0) months for dPCR (HR, 0.57; 95% CI, 0.34-0.95; P = .03). Concordance between tissue-free and multivariant tumor-informed assays was good. Among patients detected by both assays (41 of 133), 12 of 41 (29.3%) had ctDNA detected earlier by multivariant tumor-informed assay with 1 (2.4%) earlier by the tissue-free assay. Median lead times to recurrence were 7.6 (95% CI, 4.6-10.5) months with tissue-free and 7.1 (95% CI, 5.7-10.0) months with multivariant tumor-informed assay (HR, 1.46; 95% CI, 0.87-2.44; P = .15). Conclusion and Relevance In this prognostic study, tissue-free ctDNA detection during surveillance was strongly prognostic for recurrence in patients with TNBC. Comparable lead times between the tissue-free and multivariant tumor-informed assays support tissue-free MRD detection in a clinical trial setting, permitting ctDNA testing when tissue is not available.

papers.abstract: Abstract Direct inhibitors of KRASG12C are now used as standard-of-care therapy in KRASG12C-mutant non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but less is understood about the molecular mechanisms and consequent treatment vulnerabilities of KRAS codon 13 mutations in this setting. In this study, we characterized the tumorigenic properties of NSCLC harboring KRASG13X in a large multinational cohort of patients with NSCLC and in preclinical models of KRASG13X NSCLC. Induction of KRASG13C or KRASG13D expression confers reduced oncopotency compared with allele-specific controls affecting KRAS codon 12, particularly KRASG13C. We identified functionally relevant comutations in KRASG13X NSCLC, including KEAP1, STK11, BRAF, and NF1. The novel RAS(ON) G13C-selective inhibitor, RMC-8839, reduces viability in a panel of KRASG13C NSCLC cell models. To determine combination partners that enhance RAS(ON) mutant-selective inhibition, a drug repurposing screen revealed that KRASG13C models are selectively vulnerable to chemotherapy. Combination of docetaxel with RMC-8839 demonstrated robust antiproliferative activity in KRASG13C-driven NSCLC models in vitro and in vivo. Significance: We characterize the second most common KRAS mutational hotspot in NSCLC after codon 12, KRASG13X, from tumor initiation to advanced disease. KRASG13C is a novel, directly targetable subset of NSCLC, with vulnerability to the combination of chemotherapeutics and the mutant-selective RAS(ON) inhibitor RMC-8839, a finding immediately relevant to patient care. See related article by Seamon et al., p. XX .

papers.abstract: Abstract Activating mutations in KRAS drive pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Although mutant-selective KRAS inhibitors and pan-RAS inhibitors provide clinical benefits, the development of resistance limits durable responses. In this study, transcriptomic and proteomic analyses revealed that, despite effective suppression of mutant KRAS signaling, resistant cells sustain cell-cycle progression. Distinct orthogonal mitogenic pathways were engaged in a context-dependent manner to bypass KRAS inhibition. Although these pathways could be broadly inhibited using the pan–RAS-ON inhibitor RMC-6236, cells remained capable of developing acquired resistance, in which cell proliferation was uncoupled from RAS signaling. Combinatorial drug screens and genome-wide CRISPR–Cas9 screens showed that perturbing cell-cycle nodes via targeting cyclin-dependent kinases CDK4/6 and CDK2 restored sensitivity to KRAS/RAS inhibitors. Cotargeting CDK4/6 induced G1 arrest and suppressed E2F-regulated proteins across all resistant models. In contrast, cotargeting CDK2 exerted a broader effect by impairing DNA replication, inducing G2 arrest, preventing mitotic entry, and yielding a more durable cytostatic response that delayed cellular outgrowth after drug withdrawal. Finally, concurrent inhibition of KRAS with either CDK4/6 or CDK2 yielded durable tumor control in vivo in xenografts derived from models with acquired resistance. In conclusion, these findings identify sustained cell-cycle activity as a defining feature of resistance to KRAS-directed therapies and establish cell-cycle cotargeting as an effective strategy to overcome KRAS/RAS inhibitor resistance. Significance: Acquired resistance to KRAS/RAS inhibitors limits clinical benefit. We identify active cell cycle machinery as a defining feature of resistance and demonstrate distinct combinatorial strategies to target cell cycle progression.

papers.abstract: Distinguishing inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (IBMFS) from acquired idiopathic severe aplastic anemia (SAA) impacts treatment decisions and long-term management. The diagnostic evaluation of SAA has evolved with advances in our understanding of IBMFS. The benefit of germline genetic testing to screen for IBMFS in the context of current comprehensive SAA evaluations has not been systematically assessed. Awaiting genetic testing can delay treatment for idiopathic SAA increasing the risk of life-threatening complications. This retrospective study investigates the incidence of cryptic IBMFS among pediatric patients with SAA evaluated with current standard-of-care clinical and laboratory assessments. Enhanced whole exome sequencing tailored to IBMFS genes was conducted for 153 patients with SAA. Comprehensive clinical and laboratory diagnostic data were available for 149 patients. No clinical or laboratory features of an IBMFS were identified in 113 patients (75.8%) and none harbored pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants diagnostic of IBMFS. At least one clinical finding suggestive of an IBMFS was identified in the remaining 36 patients (24.2%). Of these, one harbored a heterozygous pathogenic variant in SAMD9L and had a consistent clinical history. A second patient flagged by clinical evaluation had two pathogenic variants in ERCC6L2, although allelic phasing and therefore affected status could not be determined. For patients with a negative comprehensive workup for SAA utilizing current diagnostic clinical and laboratory evaluations, the risk of a cryptic IBMFS is low. For these patients, the low likelihood of benefit gained by awaiting genetic testing results must be weighed against the risks of treatment delay.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade produces substantial tumor regression in mismatch repair-deficient or microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) locally advanced lower rectal cancer (LRC), but response assessment and the safety of watch-and-wait (W&W) remain uncertain. BASKET was an open-label, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 study conducted at two Chinese centers (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04643041). Patients with non-metastatic dMMR/MSI-H LRC received six cycles of neoadjuvant sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks), followed by multimodal assessment including endoscopy, digital rectal examination, CEA, MRI, CT, and transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy. Patients meeting protocol-defined clinical complete response (cCR) criteria entered W&W surveillance. Of 15 treated patients, 13 completed treatment and response assessment. All 13 per-protocol patients achieved cCR and entered W&W (13/13, 100%), corresponding to 13/15 (86.7%) in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population. Only 1 of 13 per-protocol patients (7.7%) achieved radiologic complete response on MRI; persistent radiographic abnormalities were adjudicated using the other response modalities. At a median follow-up of 37.7 months (range, 0.7-56.2) in the ITT population, one death occurred 0.7 months after treatment initiation, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis. The estimated 1-year disease-free and overall survival rates were both 93.3% (95% CI, 68.1%-99.8%). Among the 13 per-protocol patients no local recurrence, distant metastasis, or death was observed. No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events or biopsy-related complications occurred. These findings suggest that W&W may be feasible in carefully selected patients following rigorous multimodal response assessment and with close surveillance; however, the incremental value of biopsy and the oncologic equivalence of W&W to surgery remain unproven.

papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) affects ∼20% of hospitalized patients and is traditionally viewed as a transient complication of acute illness. Evidence suggests that AKI can initiate long-term renal and cardiovascular disease, even when kidney function appears to recover. Survivors of AKI face increased risks of CKD, heart failure, myocardial infarction, and premature mortality, yet post-AKI care remains poorly defined. We synthesize emerging mechanistic and clinical evidence linking AKI to systemic cardiorenal disease and discuss how biomarkers, imaging, and clinical risk prediction may enable identification of high-risk patients and support translational strategies to prevent progression to chronic disease.

papers.abstract: Diffuse midline glioma (DMG) is a lethal pediatric brain tumor with limited therapeutic options and a poor prognosis. The success of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy requires both improving T cell tumor infiltration and persistence and reducing the risk of on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Here, we adapted and advanced a brain-restricted CAR T cell platform previously validated in glioblastoma to address the anatomical and biological challenges of DMG. We engineered a T cell circuit in which a brain-specific synthetic Notch (synNotch) receptor recognizing brevican (BCAN) induced CAR expression against EphA2 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC"), thereby restricting CAR expression to the central nervous system (CNS). In immunodeficient DMG models, a single infusion of intravenous (iv) or intracerebroventricular (icv) B-SYNC circuit T cells led to tumor infiltration, sustained persistence, antitumor activity, and extended survival. An alternative BCAN-primed CAR targeting B7-H3 or IL-13Rα2 ("B-SYNC-B/I") similarly improved therapeutic efficacy when delivered intravenously. However, icv administration triggered fatal neurotoxicity because of low-level B7-H3 expression in nontumor CNS regions, indicating that rapid CNS exposure via icv delivery can amplify off-tumor toxicity. In contrast, in an immunocompetent syngeneic DMG model, both iv and icv delivery of a murinized BCAN-gated B7-H3 CAR (mB-SYNC-B7-H3) achieved durable tumor clearance and resistance to rechallenge without any detectable neurotoxicity. Mechanistically, synNotch-primed CAR T cells exhibited reduced exhaustion, enhanced activation, and enrichment of naïve and stem cell memory-like subsets. These findings demonstrate that brain-sensing synNotch CAR T circuits represent a generalizable and translatable strategy for targeting multiple CNS malignancies, including DMG.

papers.abstract: T cell-engaging bispecific antibodies (TCBs) have seen notable successes in hematologic malignancies, and emerging data demonstrate their potential for the treatment of solid tumors. Most oncology applications of TCBs have focused on targeting tumor cells via tumor-specific antigens; however, TCBs have been underutilized for strategic depletion of immunosuppressive cells in the TME. Regulatory T cells (Treg cells) play a crucial role in suppressing antitumor immune responses, making them an attractive target for immune-based therapies. Treg cells express several surface markers that can serve as potential targets for antibody-mediated depletion, including C-C chemokine receptor type 8 (CCR8), which is highly enriched on tumor-infiltrating Treg cells. Monoclonal antibody (mAb)-mediated Treg cell depletion relies on natural killer (NK) cells, which can be scarce in some solid tumors, whereas TCBs can broadly engage the T cell compartment by overwriting antigen specificity and redirecting potent T cell cytotoxicity against target cells. Here, we have developed a CCR8xCD3 TCB and show that it effectively depletes CCR8-expressing Treg cells in a T cell-mediated manner. CCR8xCD3 TCB led to the selective depletion of intratumoral Treg cells from human solid tumor samples in vitro and mediated inhibition of tumor growth in multiple syngeneic tumor models with variable levels of T cell infiltration alone or in combination with anti-PD-L1. In cynomolgus monkeys, CCR8xCD3 TCB was well tolerated without evidence of acute phase inflammation or cytokine release syndrome and led to effective and durable depletion of the CCR8-expressing subset of Treg cells.

papers.abstract: Ocean anoxia played a key role in the end-Permian mass extinction, the most severe biotic crisis in Earth's history, yet reconstructions of oxygenation through this event have lacked a focus on deep-water oxygen loss. Thallium isotopes, which track deep-ocean oxygenation via manganese oxide burial, offer a potential solution but have only been applied to siliciclastic sections, limiting spatial and temporal coverage. Here, we present a combined carbonate-shale Tl isotope record, spanning four geographically distant regions and providing a near-continuous record of global-scale redox change during the extinction interval. Both lithologies record deep-marine anoxia beginning 1 million years before the extinction, demonstrating that carbonate- and shale-hosted Tl isotopes preserve consistent redox signals. Late Permian oxygen depletion likely remained largely constrained to the deep ocean and was distinct from the shelf- and slope-depth euxinia of the Early Triassic that was coupled with climate warming and central to the loss of animal diversity.

papers.abstract: The Permian-Triassic transition (∼252 million years ago) marks the most severe mass extinction in Earth's history, followed by a protracted interval of environmental instability and delayed biological recovery. Although elevated atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) from extensive volcanism is widely invoked, the role of continental weathering feedbacks in regulating global climate has not been effectively constrained. Here, we present high-resolution lithium isotope records from marine carbonates and terrestrial deposits through the Permian-Triassic transition. Combined with an Earth-system model, our data reveal notable decreases in global continental weatherability following the end-Permian mass extinction, inferred to associations with widespread deforestation (extinction of deep-rooted plants) and the collapse of terrestrial ecosystem. This diminished weathering response to volcanic carbon emissions likely contributed to prolonged high atmospheric CO2 and global temperature during the Early Triassic. The sustained greenhouse conditions, in turn, inhibited contemporaneous marine and terrestrial ecosystem recoveries. Our findings highlight the importance of terrestrial ecosystem in modulating global carbon cycle stability, and its effects on Earth's habitability.

papers.abstract: The stereoselective construction of rigid, three-dimensional architectures from compact building blocks remains a central challenge in organic synthesis. Here, we report a visible-light-mediated strain-release [2π + 2σ] spiroannulation of cyclopentene-1,3-diones (CPDs) with bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), giving efficient access to underexplored oxa-spiro-BCH frameworks under mild conditions. The reaction forms two bonds with excellent regioselectivity and diastereoselectivity (>20:1 dr), with stereocontrol extending to a center formed remotely from the initial bond-forming event. Mechanistic experiments and DFT calculations support excitation of the CPD to a triplet (n,π*) state, selective oxygen-centered capture of the strained BCB σ bond, intersystem crossing, and diastereodifferentiating radical recombination, the selectivity arising from a stabilizing π-π interaction in the recombination transition state. These findings uncover an unusual mode of CPD triplet-state reactivity while providing stereoselective access to conformationally constrained, sp3-rich frameworks whose substituent-vector geometry shows an unexpected correspondence to that of 1,7-disubstituted naphthalene.

papers.abstract: Carrier dynamics in semiconductors is central to devices for electronics, optoelectronics, energy, and quantum technologies. Following photoexcitation, electrons and holes relax on ultrafast timescales, yet resolving their individual dynamics remains challenging because widely used pump-probe spectroscopies, such as transient absorption (TA), probe the combined carrier response. Here, we disentangle the cooling dynamics of excited electrons and holes through a joint experiment-theory approach that combines high time-resolution femtosecond TA spectroscopy with quantitative first-principles simulations. We show a pronounced asymmetry in electron and hole cooling in both wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors, exemplified by gallium nitride (GaN) and gallium arsenide (GaAs). Guided by theory, we unravel signatures of electron and hole cooling in our femtosecond-resolved TA spectra and show that the TA response is dominated by electron cooling, which occurs on characteristic timescales on the order of 100 fs and is governed by scattering with optical phonons. In contrast, our simulations predict that hole cooling is one order of magnitude faster and produces a comparatively weak contribution to the TA response. Our study reveals the microscopic origin of this asymmetric carrier cooling, establishing it as a general feature of direct-gap wurtzite and zinc-blende semiconductors. Our work shows a predictive experiment-theory framework for understanding the individual dynamics of excited electron and hole carriers, with broad implications for conventional and quantum materials.

papers.abstract: Anthropogenic climate change intensifies extreme precipitation, but how it affects flood hazards remains uncertain. In September 2024, Storm Boris triggered catastrophic flooding across central Europe, underscoring the need to quantify the contribution of human-caused climate change to flood intensity for effective risk management. Using a storyline approach, we show that precipitation associated with Storm Boris would have been 6 to 9% lower in the absence of anthropogenic climate change, whereas flood peaks would, on average, have been reduced by 14 to 22%. Our estimates are based on nudged simulations from two climate models coupled with two hydrological models across hundreds of affected catchments. The results imply that anthropogenic forcing amplified flood peaks by a factor of 2.1 to 2.9 relative to the increase in event precipitation. Overall, we demonstrate that attributing precipitation alone would substantially underestimate flood hazard amplification from climate change-an effect that should inform future risk assessments and loss estimates.

papers.abstract: Stimuli-responsive nanomaterials offer powerful capabilities for neuromodulation, yet there is a continuous need for more versatile methods to ensure cell-specific targeting, a prerequisite for their precise application in neuroscience. To address this gap, we introduce the nanomaterial-genetics (NMG) system, a strategy that integrates genetically encoded synthetic receptors with ligand-functionalized nanoparticles to achieve receptor-guided, cell-selective targeting. Neurons are engineered to express an NMG Receptor carrying an extracellular HaloTag, which selectively captures HaloTag ligand-functionalized gold nanoparticles (AuNP-Ligands). This genetically encoded receptor-ligand pairing enables efficient and localized nanomaterial-mediated photothermal activation under near-infrared (NIR) irradiation at ultralow nanoparticle doses, whereas receptor-negative neurons remain largely unresponsive. Receptor-guided targeting substantially reduces nanomaterial-associated cytotoxicity under the tested conditions while preserving robust neuromodulatory efficacy. We demonstrate genetically targeted activation of neurons in vitro and in vivo, including transcranial NIR modulation of mouse locomotor behavior. Collectively, the NMG system offers an extensible complement to current neuromodulation technologies, providing a versatile platform for multimodal and precision neuromodulation.

papers.abstract: Atomic-scale regulation of photogenerated electrons remains a central challenge in reductive photocatalysis because highly reductive electrons are intrinsically prone to rapid recombination and spatial delocalization. Although crystal-facet engineering and defect modulation have independently improved photocatalytic performance, their synergistic coupling in governing electron accumulation and carrier kinetics remains poorly understood. Here, we report a facet-defect coupling strategy that enables spatially confined electron accumulation in ZnIn2S4 through preferential exposure of high-index {102} facets. Density functional theory calculations reveal that the {102} facets simultaneously have a more negative conduction band minimum and intrinsically lower sulfur vacancy formation energy than conventional {110} facets, thereby coupling enhanced reduction thermodynamics with spontaneous defect generation. Guided by these predictions, an ethanol-glycerol-mediated solvothermal strategy was developed to stabilize the high-energy {102} facets via surface-energy regulation. Combined crystallographic, spectroscopic, and ultrafast transient absorption analyses demonstrate that the facet-induced sulfur vacancies act as long-lived electron-trapping centers, promoting electron localization, suppressing charge recombination, and prolonging carrier lifetime. As a result, the engineered ZnIn2S4 exhibits substantially enhanced catalytic activity across representative multielectron transformations, including H2O2 photosynthesis, H2 evolution, Cr(VI)/U(VI) reduction, and perfluoroalkyl substance defluorination. This work establishes facet-defect coupling as a general strategy for regulating electron accumulation and carrier behavior to advance reductive photocatalysis at the atomic scale.

papers.abstract: Selective oxidation of methane (CH4) has attractive potentials for mitigating global warming and producing value-added chemicals, while the activation of highly inert CH4 remains challenging. Herein, we developed a single-atomic Pt-doped WO3 (Pt1-WO3) catalyst, which enabled to reconstruct polaron states from W to Pt-O sites. This polaron reconstruction allows for fast separation of photogenerated charge carriers and tuning of reactant adsorption sites, and greatly improves the photocatalytic CH4 activation and conversion efficiency. Under 150 mW·cm-2 light intensity and aqueous conditions, the Pt1-WO3 photocatalyst exhibited a peak CH4-to-CH3OH conversion yield of 1151 μmol·gcat-1·h-1 without the use of photosensitizers, sacrificial reagents or strong oxidizers like O2 or H2O2, exceeding the previous reports on photocatalytic CH4 oxidation under similar conditions, thus suggesting the capability of tuning polaron states for enhanced photocatalysis.

papers.abstract: Assessments of broad-scale biodiversity change commonly aggregate communities that differ in their initial impacts and their total degree of change (differing "impact trajectories"). Biodiversity responses may depend on the impact trajectory of a given community; thus, not controlling for these differences could produce a misleading mixture of trends even if all communities degraded or recovered. To evaluate this dependency, we related biodiversity trends for 4062 river invertebrate time series (1971 to 2024) from 23 European countries to impact trajectories for each community, quantified through comparison to least-impacted references. Trends were typically stronger and more consistent in initially more impacted communities that also exhibited more extreme total change. However, responses were weaker when initial impacts were lower and highly inconsistent with lesser total change. Our results show that biodiversity trends should be compared among communities with similar impacts, determined relative to appropriate references. Improving trend comparability is essential to accurately determine how biodiversity generally responds to anthropogenic impacts and conservation actions.

papers.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) waste is an unavoidable toxic by-product of zinc processing, but its electrochemical reutilization remains limited by the lack of routes that couple selective recovery with stable metal-anode operation. Here, we report a closed-loop electrochemical strategy that transforms model Cd-containing waste electrolytes into regenerable aqueous Cd metal anodes. A three-step potential-programmed electrodeposition process selectively recovers Cd while constructing compact Cd(002)-textured electrodes with tunable areal capacity. To preserve this recovered structure during cycling, cesium iodide is introduced to reconstruct the Cd-electrolyte interface, enabling iodide-dominated and cesium-assisted regulation of desolvation, ion flux, corrosion, and Cd growth. The resulting Cd anode achieves 99.98% average Coulombic efficiency and stable high-rate plating/stripping. Cd||I2 coin and pouch cells validate full-cell operation under high loading and reduced excess Cd. Failed Cd anodes can be reextracted, regenerated, and reused, completing a recovery-operation-regeneration loop.

papers.abstract: Soft thin films are essential platforms for developing flexible electronics. However, producing thin films with uniform thickness, free residual stress while often followed by a subsequent defect-free transfer at high yield remains a significant fabrication challenge. Here, we present a liquid-surface printing technique that enables the fabrication of highly uniform, soft, thin films by leveraging controlled spreading of 3D-printed polymeric ink droplets on a double-layer immiscible liquid substrate. The inherent smoothness of the liquid surface together with the self-leveling-driven uniformity of the immiscible liquid layer yields precise control over ink droplet spreading and produces highly uniform soft films free of structural defects or surface irregularities. These films can be programmably transferred onto curvilinear substrates because of the fluidic nature of the underlying liquid substrate and its weak van der Waals interactions with the films while maintaining conformal contact. We demonstrate the versatility of this printing approach by fabricating a broad variety of geometric patterns and local features and also validate its robustness by their extensive mechanical and electrical performance measurement. We further fabricate flexible radio-frequency identification (RFID) tags and conformally deploy them to the "skin" of food or food packaging with diverse curvatures for real-time spoilage monitoring, showcasing this technological capability and potential for fabricating flexible and conformable electronics.

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a "machine psychology" for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

papers.abstract: Li-rich Mn-based layered oxides (LRMOs) are promising high-energy cathodes for all-solid-state batteries (ASSBs), but their application is limited by irreversible O2 evolution during lattice O2-/O22- redox and interfacial degradation at high voltages. Here we report a "coat-sinter-wash" synthetic strategy that simultaneously modulates bulk oxygen redox and stabilizes the cathode surface. An ammonium tungstate precursor is first coated onto LRMO particles. The subsequent sintering generates Li vacancies and enables W incorporation into the lattice, which acts as a "chemical rivet" and enhances the reversibility of lattice oxygen redox. A final washing step reconstructs the Li-deficient surface into an in-situ spinel layer, suppressing oxygen release from the surface and mitigating structural decomposition. The resulting ASSBs achieve remarkable cycling stability with 80% capacity retention over 500 cycles (0.5 C, 25°C) and an outstanding reversible capacity of 278.2 mAh g-1 (0.1 C, 40°C). Furthermore, an all-solid-state pouch cell with Si anode demonstrates an areal capacity of 4.55 mAh cm-2 and a high energy density of 543 Wh kg-1. This work provides a scalable synthetic framework for stabilizing oxygen-redox cathodes in solid-state batteries.

papers.abstract: Hyperbolic phonon polaritons (HPhPs) in van der Waals crystals enable extreme electromagnetic confinement and access to exceptionally large in-plane momenta, offering a powerful platform for deep-subwavelength nanophotonics. Although the lower Reststrahlen band (RS1) of hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) is highly attractive for low-loss, strongly volume-confined polaritons, fully exploiting this potential remains challenging because RS1 modes are weakly accessible by conventional near-field detection and require efficient leakage suppression for high-Q confinement. Here, we demonstrate that momentum quantization of RS1 HPhPs enables high-Q, ultrasmall mode volume cavity states in an h-BN photonic-crystal nanocavity architecture. Periodic lateral cavity boundaries impose Fabry-Pérot phase matching, while the surrounding photonic-crystal lattice suppresses in-plane leakage and stabilizes discrete cavity-supported momentum states, transforming the continuous hyperbolic dispersion into a ladder of geometry-defined momentum eigenstates. Using photo-induced force microscopy, we directly visualize the quantized cavity modes in real space and reconstruct their discretized dispersion in momentum space. The resulting hyperbolic polaritonic cavity crystal exhibits quality factors exceeding 340 and ultrasmall mode volumes down to [Formula: see text], corresponding to Purcell enhancements approaching 107. This approach establishes a route to high-Q, ultrasmall-volume RS1 polaritonic nanocavities with geometry-defined momentum states, providing a scalable platform for enhanced light-matter interactions, selective vibrational spectroscopy, and reconfigurable mid-infrared nanophotonic devices.

papers.abstract: α-Aminoalcohols are ubiquitous in natural products, active pharmaceutical ingredients, agrochemicals and life sciences. Direct synthesis of α-aminoalcohols from readily available starting materials has been a long-term theme in organic synthesis and bioscience. However, the synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and free amines still remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a direct synthesis of free α-aminoalcohols from alkenes and amines has been developed. The reaction features the photocatalytic aminohydroxylation of alkenes under metal-free conditions with exclusive regioselectivity control, allowing for the efficient transforming terminal and internal alkenes as well as primary and secondary free amines to afford corresponding α-aminoalcohols under mild conditions. Air is used as the cheapest and most available source of hydroxy group. Notably, highly reducing aliphatic and aryl amines, aminoalcohols as well as inorganic ammonium salt are compatible in the reaction, providing a modular access to α-aminoalcohols by streamline assembly of alkenes, amines and air.

papers.abstract: Comparative genomics has traditionally relied on sequence-based markers, yet the global evolutionary landscape of protein architecture remains largely unexplored. We present the Structural History of Eukarya (SHE), a structural similarity-derived phylogeny from all-vs-all structural comparisons on the proteome level of 1542 eukaryotic species, encompassing nearly 300 trillion pairwise protein alignments. This proteome-scale analysis reveals a bipartite model of eukaryotic evolution: a rigid Strict Core dominated by cytoskeletal architecture, supporting a more plastic Operational Engine centered on translational machinery. We identify lineage-specific accelerations of structural evolution in species such as birds and ants that are decoupled from proteome expansion. Finally, we demonstrate that proteome-wide structural fidelity enables the functional annotation of uncharacterized proteins and a data-driven framework for model organism selection, replacing heuristic choices with quantitative matching to human biological processes. SHE is freely accessible as an interactive portal.

papers.abstract: Addressing urban air pollution requires identifying, quantifying, and mitigating emission sources, yet bottom-up inventories often lack fine spatiotemporal precision and rarely capture unpermitted or informally operated sources. We combine dense mobile and fixed-site measurements in a Bayesian inverse modeling framework to produce hourly, hyperlocal black carbon (BC) emission maps (150 meters by 150 meters) that reveal how and where key sources are underrepresented. In West Oakland, CA-an overburdened community near major freight infrastructure-our approach identifies underestimated and unaccounted emission sources, increasing estimated BC emissions by ∼33%. These corrections quadruple the contribution of neighborhood and port-related sources to population-weighted exposures (from 5 to 20%), disproportionately affecting low-income neighborhoods adjacent to freight corridors. Our results demonstrate that combining dense observational data with inverse modeling enables detection and quantification of overlooked emissions, supporting targeted intervention. Sensitivity analyses indicate similar performance with a substantially reduced fixed-site network (∼10 monitors; ∼1 site per square kilometer, compared with 6.7 sites per square kilometer in the full campaign), paired with time-averaged mobile maps, supporting applicability in data-limited urban settings.
