papers.abstract: Monoclonal protein is frequently tested in marginal zone lymphoma, but interpretation is often inconsistent in practice because prior studies used selective testing and rarely linked serologic findings to biology or post-treatment dynamics. We analyzed 235 adults with newly diagnosed MZL receiving first-line systemic therapy at a single center (2010-2025). All patients had baseline serum protein electrophoresis, immunofixation, and free light chain testing. Plasmacytic differentiation was reviewed by hematopathologists. M-protein response (IMWG criteria) was assessed in patients with post-treatment data. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Baseline M-protein was detected in 117 of 235 patients (49.8%), most commonly immunoglobulin M (IgM) (65.8%). M-protein positivity was associated with a higher frequency of plasmacytic differentiation (39.6% vs. 16.2%; adjusted OR 3.78). M-protein-positive patients had shorter PFS than M-protein-negative patients (median, 50.9 months vs. not reached; log-rank p = 0.044), and this association remained in multivariable analysis (hazard ratio [HR] 1.58). Overall survival (OS), progression of disease within 24 months (POD24), and histologic transformation did not differ significantly by M-protein status. Among 70 patients with evaluable post-treatment data, M-protein response of at least partial response (PR) was highly specific for clinical response and had a high positive predictive value, but response depth did not predict PFS. In uniformly tested MZL patients requiring systemic therapy, baseline M-protein identifies a subgroup enriched for plasmacytic differentiation and associated with shorter PFS. Post-treatment M-protein decline can support response confirmation when present, but it should not be used as a surrogate endpoint for durable disease control without prospective validation.

papers.abstract: Cuproptosis arises from mitochondrial copper overload, yet how tumour cells evade this metabolic vulnerability remains unclear. We identify ATP7B as the central barrier to cuproptosis in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC). ATP7B is aberrantly upregulated in PDAC and predicts poor prognosis. Its depletion increases intracellular copper, activates FDX1, DLAT/DLST lipoylation, disrupts tricarboxylic acid (TCA) metabolism, and reinstates cuproptosis in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, ATP7B undergoes ZBTB10-driven K63-linked ubiquitination, recognized by NBR1 for selective autophagic degradation. Leveraging this, we developed an ATP7B-targeting autophagy-targeting chimera (ATAUTAC) that promotes ATP7B clearance, amplifies copper-driven mitochondrial metabolic perturbations, triggers cuproptosis, and inhibits tumour growth with favourable tolerability. Notably, ATAUTAC sensitizes PDAC to gemcitabine, overcoming resistance by exposing latent metabolic fragility. These findings establish ATP7B as a mechanistic hub of cuproptosis tolerance and demonstrate that autophagy-based ATP7B degradation is a druggable strategy for copper-dependent tumour eradication. ATAUTAC offers a promising avenue for precision therapy in PDAC and other refractory malignancies.

papers.abstract: Rehabilitation is increasingly recognized as an essential component of oncology care, but there remains limited evidence regarding its broader impact on patient outcomes. This study examined the associations of inpatient cancer rehabilitation with survival and post-discharge healthcare utilization among patients with diverse cancer types. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using cancer registry-linked claims data from designated cancer care hospitals in Osaka Prefecture, Japan. The study cohort comprised adults newly diagnosed with cancer from 2020 to 2022. The exposure was receipt of inpatient cancer rehabilitation during the initial cancer treatment hospitalization. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 1 year of diagnosis, and the secondary outcomes were unplanned readmissions and out-of-hours outpatient visits within 28 days of discharge. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models were used, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors. Among 123,955 patients from 69 hospitals, 20,561 (16.6%) underwent inpatient cancer rehabilitation. Rehabilitation was associated with a lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval, 0.79-0.87). Lower mortality risks were also observed for the following cancer types: lung, upper gastrointestinal, colorectal, hepato-biliary-pancreatic, breast, and hematologic cancers. Among 115,046 patients included in the post-discharge healthcare utilization analyses, rehabilitation was associated with lower risks of unplanned readmissions (subdistribution hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval, 0.73-0.85) and out-of-hours visits (0.92; 0.84-0.999). Inpatient cancer rehabilitation was associated with lower mortality and reduced post-discharge healthcare utilization. These findings support the further integration of rehabilitation into routine oncology practice.

papers.abstract: As populations age, older adults represent a growing proportion of patients with cancer nearing the end of life. However, age-related differences in treatment decision-making and patterns of end-of-life care in routine cancer practice remain insufficiently described. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults with cancer who received palliative care consultations at a tertiary hospital in Korea between 2018 and 2022. Clinical data were linked with national health insurance claims. Patients were categorized into five age groups (18-44, 45-64, 65-74, 75-84, and ≥ 85 years), and age-related differences in referral timing, decision-making roles, and end-of-life care patterns were examined. Among 6151 patients, 54.3% were aged ≥ 65 years, including 3.3% who were aged ≥ 85 years. Older patients were referred earlier. Advance statements were completed by 59.2% overall, with the lowest completion (52.2%) and fewer patient-determined decisions to withhold or withdraw life-sustaining treatment (62.0%) in the oldest group. Intensive care unit admission rates were similar across age groups, while cardiopulmonary resuscitation and ventilation were less frequent among patients aged ≥ 85 years. Hospice use declined with age. Total medical costs during the last 6 months of life decreased with age yet remained considerable among older patients. Most deaths occurred in tertiary hospitals (26.9%-31.9%), while deaths in nursing care facilities increased with advancing age. Although older adults were referred earlier to palliative care, they were less likely to make their own treatment decisions, and aggressive care remained common. These findings indicate a need for age-sensitive approaches to improve end-of-life care.

papers.abstract: Precision oncology is based on comprehensive molecular characterization of a patient's tumor. This is mostly realized by next-generation sequencing panels or exome sequencing. Data on the value of genome sequencing from formalin-fixed paraffin embedded (FFPE) material in a clinical setting is still scarce. In this pilot, we generated datasets of matched exome and genome sequencing of FFPE tumor samples from 15 cancer patients to benchmark quality metrics, clinical feasibility, and added value for a molecular tumor board. Despite the reduced sequencing depth, diagnostic detection of small nucleotide variations, copy number variations, and complex biomarkers was maintained in genome sequencing compared to exome sequencing with the exception of hard-to-sequence regions. Evaluation by the local molecular tumor board identified additional treatment recommendations with high priority in 20% (3/15) of patients and additional molecular markers to support existing treatment recommendations in another 20% (3/15) of patients. Our work underscores the diagnostic superiority of genome sequencing even for FFPE samples and therefore supports its integration into clinical practice.

papers.abstract: Treatment intensification with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) combined with docetaxel, an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor, or selected triplet regimens is recommended for eligible patients with metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer (mCSPC). Despite increasing adoption, implementation remains variable in routine clinical practice. To characterize temporal trends in first-line systemic treatment for mCSPC and identify factors associated with receipt of guideline-concordant treatment intensification using exploratory explainable machine learning. National treatment patterns were evaluated using the Pfizer Oncology Quality Care Insight Tool derived from IQVIA Anonymized Patient Longitudinal Data, and institutional patterns were evaluated within Avera Health. The exploratory cohort included 42 patients with documented mCSPC treated between 2018 and 2023. Guideline-concordant treatment intensification was defined as ADT combined with docetaxel or a novel hormonal therapy within 90 days of ADT initiation. Potential outcome-derived variables were excluded before modeling. Six predictive approaches were evaluated using repeated nested stratified cross-validation, with 5-fold outer cross-validation repeated 20 times and 5-fold inner cross-validation repeated three times. Recursive feature elimination was performed within outer training folds, and class imbalance was addressed using SMOTE within resampling. Thirty-two (32) of forty-two (42) patients (76.2%) received guideline-concordant treatment intensification. Treatment-pattern analysis showed increasing use of first-line novel hormonal therapy and declining ADT monotherapy over time. Under repeated nested validation, discrimination was modest and variable across models. The Decision Tree achieved the highest patient-level AUC (0.675; 95% CI, 0.421-0.929), whereas Random Forest achieved an AUC of 0.650 (95% CI, 0.383-0.917), accuracy of 85.7%, precision of 88.2%, recall of 93.8%, and F1 score of 0.909. Feature-selection stability identified insurance coverage for novel hormonal therapy as the most consistently selected predictor, followed by positive core proportion and smoking history. These three variables were retained in the final explanatory Random Forest model, and global SHAP and Random Forest importance analysis showed broadly concordant rankings. Treatment intensification for mCSPC increased substantially in routine practice. Repeated nested validation produced more conservative and variable performance estimates than the original single-split analysis, underscoring the exploratory nature of this small cohort. Healthcare access and selected clinical factors warrant further evaluation in larger, multicenter datasets.

papers.abstract: To compare pathological complete response (pCR) across different neoadjuvant treatment strategies in patients with locally advanced esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) and to identify clinicopathological factors associated with pCR. In this single-center retrospective cohort study, 247 consecutive patients with locally advanced ESCC who underwent neoadjuvant therapy followed by radical esophagectomy between January 2024 and June 2025 were included. Patients were categorized into four treatment groups: chemotherapy alone (CT, n = 50), chemoradiotherapy (CRT, n = 38), chemotherapy plus immunotherapy (CT+IO, n = 142), and chemoradiotherapy plus immunotherapy (CRT+IO, n = 17). Pathological complete response was defined as ypT0N0. Clinicopathological characteristics were compared using χ² or Fisher's exact tests. Factors associated with pCR were evaluated using univariable and multivariable logistic regression analysis. Overall, 63 patients (25.5%) achieved pCR. The pCR rate was lower in the CT group than in the CT+IO group (6.0% vs. 26.8%). After adjustment for potential confounders, chemotherapy alone remained associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO (OR = 0.174, 95% CI, 0.046-0.658, P = 0.010). No significant differences were observed between CT+IO and either CRT or CRT+IO. Receipt of more than two neoadjuvant treatment cycles was associated with higher odds of pCR (OR = 2.764, 95% CI, 1.372-5.565, P = 0.004). Compared with cT3 disease, cT2 disease was associated with higher odds of pCR (OR = 3.049, 95% CI, 1.356-6.857, P = 0.007). Neoadjuvant treatment regimen, the number of neoadjuvant treatment cycles, and pretreatment clinical T stage were associated with pathological complete response in locally advanced ESCC. Chemotherapy alone was associated with lower odds of pCR than CT+IO, whereas receipt of more than two treatment cycles was associated with higher odds of pCR. These findings provide real-world evidence regarding factors associated with pathological response.

papers.abstract: Patients with metastatic melanoma who progress on standard of care therapy have limited treatment options. This study evaluates the efficacy of nivolumab combined with temozolomide compared to temozolomide alone in this refractory setting. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 44 patients with metastatic melanoma who progressed on prior immunotherapy and systemic therapies. Patients were chemotherapy-naïve and treated at a single center between 2020-2025. Endpoints included objective response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate (CBR), overall survival (OS), and progression-free survival (PFS). Patients treated with nivolumab/temozolomide had improved CBR by over fourfold compared with temozolomide alone. (OR 4.276, 95% CI:1.198-15.268; p=0.025). Median OS was 11.8 months (95% CI: 6.02, NA) with nivolumab/temozolomide versus 5.49 months (95% CI: 1.91-8.97) with monotherapy. Combination therapy was also associated with a lower hazard of death (HR 0.44; 95% CI: 0.205-0.923; p=0.030) and trended toward a lower hazard of progression (HR; 0.531 CI: 0.280-1.008; p=0.053). Exploratory analysis showed a significant treatment-LDH interaction was identified for OS (p=0. 043). Within the subgroup of patients with a baseline LDH over 2 times the upper limit of normal, combination therapy was associated with a significantly reduced hazard of death (HR: 0.183; 95% CI: 0.049-0.690; p=0.012) and progression (HR: 0.205; 95% CI: 0.060-0.692; p=0.011). Nivolumab/temozolomide had numerically higher ORR (36% vs. 10.5%, p=0.053). Combination therapy demonstrated a significantly higher CBR among patients with BRAF mutations compared to monotherapy (90.0% vs. 20.0%, p=0.017). Nivolumab and temozolomide combination therapy may represent a viable salvage regimen for refractory melanoma.

papers.abstract: To investigate utility of a novel ratio, lymphocyte to C-reactive protein ratio (LCR), for improved prognostic stratification in RCC. We conducted a retrospective machine learning-based analysis in a multicenter RCC cohort who underwent surgery (Radical or Partial Nephrectomy). Cut-off for "low" or "high" LCR was delineated by receiver operating characteristics/area under curve (ROC/AUC). Multivariable Analysis was conducted for predictors of all-cause mortality (ACM) and cancer-specific mortality (CSM). LCR, along with UCLA Integrated Staging System (UISS) factors, were included into MVA model to evaluate CSM. Employing Classification and Regression Tree (CART), we developed a decision tree based on hazard ratios (HR). The predictive performance was calculated using ROC/AUC. We analyzed 2071 patients [low LCR n=598/high LCR n=1473; cut-off=237.87 (AUC = 0.80)], median follow-up 60 months). Low LCR is an independent risk factor for ACM (HR = 2.75, p 2.0 (high-risk)]. AUC of 0.91 was revealed for the modified UISS model (AUC = 0.85 in the classic UISS model). Our findings are limited by retrospective design. This study provides evidence supporting the prognostic significance of LCR in RCC. While low LCR was associated with poorer survival outcomes, incorporating LCR into the UISS model enhanced prognostic stratification in RCC patients. Further investigation is requisite to validate our findings.

papers.abstract: Oral lichen planus (OLP) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the oral mucosa classified as a potentially malignant oral disease. However, its risk of malignant transformation remains controversial because of heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and methodologies across studies. To assess the malignant transformation rate of non-dysplastic OLP through a systematic review and meta-analysis of longitudinal studies. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines and registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261295782). PubMed, Embase, and grey literature were searched. Longitudinal observational studies including patients with histopathologically diagnosed OLP, without epithelial dysplasia at diagnosis, and reporting malignant transformation rates were included. The review focused specifically on longitudinal evidence evaluating malignant transformation in patients meeting these eligibility criteria. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and meta-analysis was performed using a random-effects model. Twenty-four studies, comprising 13, 143 patients and 230 cases of malignant transformation, were included. The pooled malignant transformation rate was 1.56% (95% CI: 1.14-2.12%), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 74.8%). Subgroup analyses showed no significant differences according to study design, geographic region, or diagnostic criteria. Meta-regression identified the male-to-female ratio as a significant moderator, while sample size and follow-up duration had no significant influence. No evidence of publication bias was observed. The malignant transformation rate of OLP was very low, with a pooled estimate of 1.56%, supporting continued surveillance. Future research should focus on standardized diagnostic approaches and reliable risk stratification models to improve understanding of malignant transformation in OLP and ensure better population representation. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261295782, identifier CRD420261295782.

papers.abstract: With accumulating evidence confirming that postoperative adjuvant radiotherapy improves survival outcomes in patients with left-sided breast cancer, the long-term cardiotoxicity risks associated with radiotherapy have attracted widespread attention. The deep inspiration breath hold (DIBH) technique increases the distance between the heart and the breast target, effectively reducing radiation dose to the heart and coronary arteries. However, the resource-intensive nature of DIBH and substantial heterogeneity in therapeutic benefits among patients pose a major clinical challenge: how to accurately and efficiently identify patients suitable for DIBH. This narrative review summarizes current evidence regarding DIBH patient selection, and integrates available strategies with clinical workflows to construct a three-tiered decision-making framework encompassing feasibility assessment, indication evaluation, and clinical benefit assessment. Given the existing gaps in high-level prospective clinical evidence, three primary research directions are proposed: (1) conducting large-scale multi-center prospective cohort studies to validate the generalizability and clinical practicality of selection strategies; (2) developing an individualized normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) model integrating multi-dimensional risk factors to guide precise decision-making; and (3) implementing prospective clinical trials of artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted selection platforms to accelerate the clinical translation of intelligent selection tools. This review synthesizes current evidence on DIBH patient selection, constructs a hierarchical decision framework to provide a reference for clinical practice, and delineates directions for future research.

papers.abstract: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) comprises a clinically and biologically heterogeneous group of breast cancers defined by the absence of estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor expression and the lack of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) overexpression or amplification. Although systemic treatment has expanded beyond chemotherapy to include immune checkpoint blockade, poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibition in selected patients with germline BRCA1/2 variants, and antibody-drug conjugates in advanced disease, therapeutic resistance and disease recurrence remain major challenges. Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are abundant stromal cells that contribute to the organization and function of the TNBC microenvironment. Rather than representing a single uniformly tumor-promoting population, CAFs encompass transcriptionally and functionally diverse states that vary across tumors, spatial niches, and treatment contexts. Current evidence supports roles for selected CAF populations in extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling, paracrine signaling, metabolic exchange, immune-cell positioning, and adaptation to therapeutic stress. Recent single-cell and spatial studies have further identified ECM-rich, inflammatory, hypoxia-associated, and progenitor-like fibroblast states that correlate with distinct immune landscapes and treatment responses. However, many proposed CAF markers are shared across states, nomenclature remains inconsistent among datasets, and most CAF-directed therapeutic strategies are supported primarily by preclinical evidence. This review summarizes the current understanding of CAF heterogeneity in TNBC, examines the mechanisms through which fibroblast states influence tumor progression and antitumor immunity, and critically evaluates their contribution to chemotherapy and immunotherapy resistance. Particular attention is given to the distinction between mechanistic evidence and associative transcriptomic findings, as well as to the translational challenges that must be addressed before CAF-based biomarkers or therapies can be incorporated into routine TNBC management.

papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is characterized by extensive cellular heterogeneity and complex interactions between malignant cells and the surrounding microenvironment. The contribution of neuronal populations to GBM progression and prognosis, however, remains incompletely understood. Bulk transcriptomic data from TCGA-GBM and GTEx were integrated with two single-cell RNA-seq datasets. Differential expression analysis, WGCNA, machine-learning-based survival modeling, CIBERSORT, GSEA, CopyKAT, MiloR, pseudotime analysis, GSVA, CellChat, and pySCENIC were used to characterize prognostic genes and their cellular context. PDIA4 was further examined in U251 and U87 cells using siRNA-mediated knockdown followed by Western blotting, qPCR, Transwell invasion, wound-healing, colony-formation, and CCK-8 assays. Nine prognostic genes-PDIA4, CAMK2N1, RPH3A, RAB11FIP4, DMTN, EPHB6, SLC47A2, ESM1, and EMILIN2-were retained in the final prognostic model. Single-cell analysis showed distinct cellular distributions of these genes and identified a tumor-associated neuronal population enriched in GBM. Pseudotime analysis revealed transcriptional differences between normal- and tumor-associated neuronal states, while CellChat predicted altered NRXN-NLGN communication involving neuronal populations and GBM cells. Immune deconvolution showed associations between several prognostic genes and immune-cell composition, including an inverse correlation between PDIA4 and activated NK cells. Experimentally, PDIA4 was expressed at higher levels in U251 and U87 cells than in SVG p12 cells. PDIA4 knockdown reduced clonogenic growth, invasion, wound closure, and CCK-8 metabolic activity readouts in both GBM cell lines. Integrative bulk and single-cell analyses linked GBM prognosis to distinct neuronal and immune features of the tumor microenvironment. Together, these analyses place the nine-gene prognostic signature within the cellular architecture of GBM and highlight tumor-associated neuronal states as a potential component of the prognostic tumor ecosystem. PDIA4 knockdown provided complementary functional support for one component of the signature, while the predicted NRXN-NLGN network nominates a candidate route of neuron-GBM communication for future investigation.

papers.abstract: Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), typically defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, is increasing in incidence worldwide and exhibits distinctive clinical, molecular, and environmental features compared with later-onset (LOCRC) disease. However, the tumor-immune microenvironment (TiME) of EOCRC and its implications for prevention and therapy remain poorly characterized. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on the TiME of EOCRC and contrast it with that of conventional LOCRC. We first discuss global features of the EOCRC immune landscape, including innate and adaptive immune composition, functional states, and spatial organization, highlighting areas where apparent age-related differences reflect true biology versus confounding by tumor site, stage, or mismatch repair (MMR) status. We then examine immunogenomic and epigenomic determinants-such as MMR deficiency distribution, microbial mutational signatures, chromosomal instability, and age-conditioned methylation programs-that shape neoantigen landscapes, antigen presentation, and immune evasion in younger patients. Next, we review microbiome-driven immunomodulation, focusing on dysbiosis, genotoxic bacteria, and early-life and young-adult exposures as joint modifiers of mucosal immunity and tumor development. Finally, we explore how these insights inform immune-based prevention (risk stratification, screening, diet and microbiome interventions, and chemoprevention) and immunotherapy strategies, including checkpoint blockade and rational combinations in the predominant microsatellite-stable EOCRC population.

papers.abstract: Summary Introduction Peri‐operative glucagon‐like peptide‐1 receptor agonist (GLP‐1 RA) use is associated with delayed gastric emptying. It is unclear what proportion of patients having anaesthetic care are receiving GLP‐1 RAs; what strategies are used in their peri‐operative management; and whether the incidence of pulmonary aspiration and/or regurgitation is greater in this population. Methods We performed a national prospective multicentre cohort study of adults undergoing elective or emergency procedures under the care of an anaesthetist. Patients were screened for GLP‐1 RA use in the 3 months before the index procedure. Data were collected on patient, procedure, anaesthesia and outcomes, including pulmonary aspiration and regurgitation. The primary outcome was the proportion of patients receiving GLP‐1 RAs. Secondary outcomes described the pre‐operative management of GLP‐1 RAs; anaesthesia and airway management in patients receiving GLP‐1 RAs; and the incidence of pulmonary aspiration and/or regurgitation. Results Of 47,039 patients from 119 sites across the UK, 1348 (2.9%) reported receiving GLP‐1 RAs. Peri‐operative management was variable regarding drug cessation, anaesthesia and airway management. The incidence (95%CI) of pulmonary aspiration and/or regurgitation in the non‐GLP‐1 RA cohort was 57/45,691 (0.12% (0.09–0.16%)) and in the GLP‐1 RA cohort was 19/1348 (1.41% (0.85–2.19%)); odds ratio (95%CI) 11.39 (6.47–20.05), p < 0.001. In patients receiving GLP‐1 RAs, pulmonary aspiration and/or regurgitation occurred most frequently during emergence from anaesthesia. Discussion In this national study, 1 in 36 patients undergoing anaesthesia care received GLP‐1 RAs, and their peri‐operative management was variable. A range of airway management techniques aiming to reduce pulmonary aspiration risk were observed but, despite this, the incidence of pulmonary aspiration and/or regurgitation was 1 in 71 in people receiving GLP‐1 RAs.

papers.abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted nerve tracking facilitates real-time ultrasound-guided nerve identification, but its effect on independent nerve identification after AI support is removed remains uncertain. Methods In this prospective randomized trial, 80 ultrasound novices (60 medical students and 20 anesthesiology residents) were assigned to either a control group receiving B-mode ultrasound training without AI assistance or an AI-assisted group using a real-time nerve tracking system (NerveTrack). Following a standardized lecture and a 10-minute hands-on training session, participants underwent assessment with the AI function disabled. The primary outcome was first-attempt independent identification success for the median nerve and supraclavicular brachial plexus. Secondary outcomes included performance after additional training and self-reported confidence. Results 78 participants completed the study. First-attempt independent identification success rates did not differ significantly between the control and AI-assisted groups for the median nerve (57.5% vs 65.8%; RR 1.14, 95% CI 0.81 to 1.62; p=0.452) or the brachial plexus (35.0% vs 42.1%; RR 1.20, 95% CI 0.68 to 2.11; p=0.519). Following additional AI-assisted training, participants in the AI-assisted group reported greater confidence in identifying the brachial plexus than those in the control group (4.7±0.5 vs 4.4±0.9; p=0.046). No significant differences were observed in independent identification success after additional training. Conclusions Brief AI-assisted training did not improve immediate independent ultrasound identification of the median nerve or supraclavicular brachial plexus after AI support was removed. These findings do not establish long-term retention, transfer to unfamiliar anatomy, or clinical procedural performance. The registration number NCT05857787 .

papers.abstract: Neuroendocrine differentiation (NED) promotes lineage plasticity and therapy resistance in prostate and lung cancers. Here we identify NED as a route of treatment escape in breast cancer: neuroendocrine features emerged or increased in 22% of progressive cases, predominantly, but not exclusively, in HER2-positive subtype. Using patient-derived, epithelial/neuroendocrine organoid and xenograft models, we map the epigenetic and transcriptional divergence between epithelial and neuroendocrine states arising from a shared mutational background and define a breast cancer neuroendocrine signature. NED involves epigenetic silencing of EpCAM and amplified HER2, while NEUROD1 functions as a master transcriptional regulator of the neuroendocrine fate. NCAM-positive putative circulating tumor cells were detected in patients in whom EpCAM-based detection had failed. Neuroendocrine tumor cells exhibit an FGFR1 dependency associated with NCAM-FGFR1 interaction and mesenchymal FGFR1 splicing. Together, these findings establish NED as a mechanism of escape from HER2-targeted therapy in breast cancer, with implications for disease monitoring and intervention.

papers.abstract: Breast cancers with a stiff extracellular matrix (ECM) frequently evade immune surveillance through mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify a mechanosensitive immune-evasion pathway governed by the phosphorylation-dependent prolyl isomerase Pin1. We show that ECM rigidity stabilizes Pin1 and promotes its nuclear accumulation in cancer cells, where it preserves heterochromatin organization and nuclear envelope integrity by sustaining HP1α-Lamin interactions, thereby suppressing transposable element (TE) activity. Pin1 loss induces early heterochromatin relaxation and LINE1 reactivation, activating the cGAS/STING/type I interferon pathway. Pin1 depletion further promotes TE-derived neoantigen generation and broadly remodels the tumor immune microenvironment, eliciting innate and adaptive immune responses that enhance tumor clearance. Genetic Pin1 depletion, or pharmacological inhibition with clinically available drugs, sensitizes fibrotic, immune-cold tumors to immune checkpoint blockade. These findings uncover a mechano-genomic mechanism of immune evasion in breast cancer and establish Pin1 as a therapeutic target to restore tumor immunogenicity and improve immunotherapy efficacy.

papers.abstract: To develop and validate an interpretable machine learning (ML) model that integrates extracellular volume fraction (ECV) derived from contrast-enhanced CT with clinical and imaging features for preoperative prediction of World Health Organization/International Society of Urological Pathology (WHO/ISUP) grade in clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC). A retrospective cohort of 263 patients with pathologically confirmed ccRCC from two institutions was analyzed. Patients from Hospital A (n=184) were randomly divided into training (n=128) and internal validation (n=56) cohorts, while patients from Hospital B (n=79) served as an independent external validation cohort. CT-derived ECV, arterial enhancement fraction (AEF), and conventional imaging features were extracted. Six machine learning models (Logistic Regression [LR], eXtreme Gradient Boosting [XGBoost], Gaussian Naive Bayes [GNB], Support Vector Machine [SVM], K-Nearest Neighbors [KNN], Light Gradient Boosting Machine [LightGBM]) were constructed, and the best-performing model was identified based on bootstrap resampling. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP). Tumor size (low-grade: 4.99 ± 1.98 cm; high-grade: 6.20 ± 2.72 cm, P = 0.002), ECV (low-grade: 0.46 ± 0.09; high-grade: 0.57 ± 0.12, P<0.001), and AEF (low-grade: 1.37 ± 0.24; high-grade: 1.56 ± 0.25, P<0.001) were significantly higher in high-grade ccRCC, while hematocrit (HCT, low-grade: 0.41 ± 0.05; high-grade: 0.38 ± 0.06, P<0.001) was lower. The optimal LR model achieved robust performance: training cohort AUC = 0.995 (95% CI: 0.990-0.999), internal validation AUC = 0.903 (95% CI: 0.818-0.988), external test AUC = 0.857 (95% CI: 0.756-0.958). SHAP analysis showed ECV, tumor diameter, and AEF were the top 3 predictors. An interpretable ML model incorporating CT-derived ECV and imaging features effectively predicts preoperative WHO/ISUP grade of ccRCC, providing a noninvasive tool for individualized risk stratification and clinical decision-making.

papers.abstract: Melanoma has a growing incidence, and early and accurate detection can enhance survival rates. However, its complex diagnoses pose challenges that could be overcome by Artificial Intelligence (AI), and the ABCD(E) rule (Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter, and Evolution) is a major screening pattern enabling melanoma detection. This systematic review assessed advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) for melanoma diagnosis, particularly focusing on systems incorporating or informed by ABCD(E) criteria. Guided by Cochrane and PRISMA guidelines, this review included experimental or observational studies indexed on PubMed, LILACS, Latindex, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials platforms. Independent screening and data extraction were performed by two authors. 2,735 records were assessed and 21 studies were included in the final screening, analyzing over 90,000 images/cases. AI systems, notably CNNs and DCNNs, demonstrated promising diagnostic performance, often matching or exceeding human expert evaluation, achieving an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 90.3% for early melanoma differentiation. Patient selection bias was observed, limiting applicability of the findings. AI shows significant and evolving capability in skin lesion diagnosis, increasingly integrating ABCD(E) criteria. While offering enhanced diagnostic consistency, challenges persist, including data limitations, model generalizability, and interpretability.

papers.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is a X-linked disease affecting skeletal and cardiac muscle and is caused by mutations in the dystrophin gene (DMD). Patient-derived induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) serve as reliable in vitro disease models. Their genetic correction by CRISPR/Cas9 allows the generation of isogenic controls and holds promises for gene therapy. However, restoring full-length dystrophin, especially when deletions involve multiple exons, constitutes a technological challenge. This study aimed to fully repair the dystrophin gene from a DMD iPSC line carrying the deletion of exons 49-50 and to characterize the rescue of the cardiac phenotype. We developed an innovative CRISPR/Cas9-based approach involving the insertion of coding sequences of the deleted region, at the 3' of exon 48, thereby generating a single continuous coding sequence encompassing exons 48-49-50. Subsequently, iPSCs were differentiated into cardiomyocytes and cardiac fibroblasts. Cardiac phenotypes were analysed by western blot, immunofluorescence, ELISA, FACS, Ionoptix, 3D engineered heart tissue (EHT) and single-nuclei RNA-seq. The correction of a two-exons DMD gene deletion in Duchenne iPSCs, using CRISPR/Cas9, enabled the re-expression of a stable and functional full-length dystrophin in cardiomyocytes resulting in the rescue of cardiac pathological phenotypes. Edited cardiomyocytes showed improved morphology, reduced release of the cardiomyocytes damage marker troponin I, and decreased ROS production. Moreover, dystrophin restoration enhanced contractility and ameliorated the Ca2+ kinetics. Notably, edited iPSC derived fibroblasts showed reduced pro-fibrotic stimuli response. In parallel, we also observed enhanced functioning of a 3D engineered heart tissue and profound change in the transcriptomic profile in both cardiomyocytes and fibroblasts after the re-expression of full-length dystrophin. We developed an innovative approach that enabled the re-expression of full-length dystrophin in a DMD iPSC line with consequent complete rescue of in vitro DMD cardiac phenotypes. On the long term, these results could lay a foundation for future applications of cell therapy or in vivo CRISPR/Cas9-based intervention to treat DMD.

papers.abstract: Neoadjuvant chemo-immunotherapy (NACI) demonstrates promising efficacy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA-HNSCC), yet its effect on postoperative radiotherapy/chemoradiotherapy (PORT/POCRT) remains undefined. This open-label phase 2 study (NCT05476965) assessed NACI efficacy and its role in guiding adaptive PORT/POCRT. Primary endpoint was major pathologic response (MPR) rate (0-10% residual tumor). Secondary endpoints are overall survival (OS), disease-free survival (DFS), objective response rate (ORR), and adverse events. Thirty resectable stage III-IVB HNSCC patients received sintilimab plus chemotherapy, followed by surgery and response-adapted PORT/POCRT. Patients with MPR received low-dose PORT (0-54 Gy), while patients without MPR received standard PORT/POCRT. The MPR rate was 59.1% (38.7%-76.7%). The MPR with low-dose group showed higher 2-year OS (100% vs. 77.8%) and DFS (100% vs. 55.6%) with fewer radiotherapy-related adverse events than non-MPR with standard-dose group (all P < 0.05). Adaptive radiation de-escalation maintains survival while reducing toxicity, representing a new strategy for LA-HNSCC.

papers.abstract: The oxide path mechanism offers vision possibility from kinetics for the anodic oxygen evolution reaction, yet its universal activation remains elusive due to the difficulty of constructing globally appropriate interatomic distances. Here, we address this challenge in the integrated-screened Y0.1Ir0.2Ru0.7Ox by precisely regulating the Ru-Ru1 bond length and constructing locally ordered yet long-range disordered structures that dissipate lattice strain, thereby enabling homogeneous modulation of interatomic distances across the framework. In-situ infrared spectroscopy together with online mass spectrometry confirms that the catalyst consistently follows a universal pathway. Building on these structural and mechanistic advantages, the nanostructured catalyst achieves a low cell voltage of 1.75 V@3 A cm-2 with operational stability ( > 2800 h @ 3 A cm-2, 0.0625 mV h-1 decay rate) in proton exchange membrane water electrolysis. This work establishes a generalizable framework for pervasive dual-site catalysis, providing a paradigm for next-generation water electrolysis anodes and beyond.

papers.abstract: Nucleic acid testing is important for infectious-disease diagnosis, but combining high sensitivity with accessible testing remains challenging. Here we show a chip-based visual detection strategy for one or two viral RNA targets that involves only sample loading, without further instrumentation or manual actuation. Target-activated CRISPR-Cas13a alters the wettability of a molecular barrier, causing liquid to cross a preset threshold and generate a dam-break drainage signal. The chip detects a single target at 10 aM within 2 min and two targets at 100 aM within 5 min, with costs of $0.20 and $0.30 per test, respectively. We further establish a practical clinical-sample workflow combining room-temperature lysis with RNase inhibition and validate the platform across 40 nasal-swab samples tested for SARS-CoV-2, influenza A virus and influenza B virus, with results concordant with RT-PCR. This threshold-based fluidic strategy provides a route towards rapid, low-cost and instrument-free molecular testing outside centralized laboratories.

papers.abstract: Biosecurity screening of synthetic DNA orders is a key defense against malicious actors and careless enthusiasts producing dangerous pathogens or toxins. It is important to evaluate biosecurity screening tools for potential vulnerabilities and to work responsibly with providers to ensure that vulnerabilities can be patched before being publicly disclosed. We consider a class of potential vulnerabilities in which a DNA sequence is obfuscated by splitting it into two or more fragments within a single synthetic DNA order, where the fragments can be readily reassembled via routine biological mechanisms. To evaluate this potential vulnerability, we develop a test set of obfuscated sequences based on controlled toxins, and share these materials with the biosecurity screening community. We then collect and analyze results from open-source and commercial biosecurity screening tools, alongside a novel Gene Edit Distance algorithm specifically designed to be robust against splitting-based obfuscations.

papers.abstract: Elucidating the failure mechanisms of Li metal electrodes is critical to accelerating the development of long cycle life Li metal batteries. However, it has not yet fully been realized so far due to the challenges associated with quantitative and qualitative characterization of solid electrolyte interphase on metal at large-area scale. Herein, we establish a relationship between solid byproducts and dead Li amounts in solid electrolyte interphase on Li metal by using fluorescence imaging and fluorescence titration method. The success of this methodology depends on the finding of a highly selective molecular probe, dilithium 3-hydroxy-2-naphthoate, with reversible change in fluorescence wavelength and intensity toward Li metal. Accordingly, the continuous generation of solid byproducts is acknowledged as potential underlying reason towards dead Li accumulation, determining the failure of Li electrode. These findings provide insights into the understanding of failure mechanism of Li metal electrode and design of strategies to improve its cycle life.

papers.abstract: The type VI secretion system (T6SS) is a large macromolecular complex crucial for inter-bacterial competition. Its expression and localization are tightly regulated, with the anti-bacterial H1-T6SS in Pseudomonas aeruginosa assembling in response to membrane damage. While several proteins are known to regulate this response, the mechanism remains unknown. Here, we use biochemical approaches to show formation of a complex between the membrane lipoprotein TagQ and the periplasmic protein TagR. Furthermore, Co-IP and in silico modeling indicates TagQ/R complex interactions with PpkA, likely dimerizing the kinase to initiate a phosphorylation cascade leading to H1-T6SS assembly. Mass spectrometry analysis of phosphorylated proteins in P. aeruginosa shows that PpkA does not have any targets outside of the previously reported Fha1, suggesting the sensor module acts exclusively to regulate T6SS assembly. Our work reveals the functional basis of the TagQR-PpkA signaling pathway and links membrane damage to localized H1-T6SS assembly, which is critical for efficient retaliation during inter-bacterial interactions.

papers.abstract: Polar vortices in ferroelectric heterostructures hold promise for high-density, energy-efficient nanoelectronics, but their controlled motion remains elusive due to strong pinning and lattice-coupled dynamics. Here, we report real-time observation of vortex boundary motion in PbTiO₃/SrTiO₃ heterostructures using localized trailing electric fields applied via a conductive atomic force microscopy (AFM) tip. The vortex boundaries show reversible motion that depends on both field polarity and AFM tip trajectory. By precisely steering the tip along specific paths, we achieve controlled, reconfigurable vortex boundary motion with remarkable stability over extended periods. In-situ scanning transmission electron microscopy further confirmed the controlled motion of the vortex boundary. Phase-field simulations reveal that this motion is governed by switching of the zigzag pattern at the vortex core, pinpointing the underlying physical mechanism. These results establish the feasibility of externally controlled vortex boundary motion, advancing both fundamental understanding of polar topological dynamics and prospects for next-generation polar-vortex-based nanoelectronic devices.

papers.abstract: Breeding wheat varieties with a high nitrogen use efficiency (NUE) reduces both production costs and threats to the ecological environment. Here, using candidate-gene and genome-wide association studies, we identify TaNPF7.6-A1 as a positive regulator of NUE in wheat. A widely conserved polymorphism in the coding region of TaNPF7.6-A1 produces allele TaNPF7.6-A1mod with a higher transcription level and nitrate transport activity than TaNPF7.6-A1lan, resulting in a greater NUE. We also reveal the mechanism by which TaEIL3-TaJAZ1-TaNPF7.6-A1 regulates NUE in wheat. TaNPF7.6-A1mod interacts more strongly with TaJAZ1 than TaNPF7.6-A1lan and promotes the retention of nuclear-localized TaJAZ1 in the cytoplasm. TaJAZ1 interacts with TaEIL3 and represses TaEIL3, binding to the TaNPF7.6-A1mod promoter, influencing allele expression and causing phenotypic differences. TaNPF7.6-A1mod also shows significant geographical distribution aggregation globally and undergoes continuous positive selection during the breeding process. Overall, this study provides molecular and evolutionary insights into the regulation of NUE.

papers.abstract: G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) govern diverse cellular responses and are crucial drug targets. However, the sequence of structural events from G protein recognition to GDP release has remained elusive. Here, we leveraged the viral chemokine GPCR US28 to capture multiple activation states of the US28-Gq complex. Using cryo-electron microscopy and an engineered chemokine superagonist, we determined three distinct complex structures, capturing a GDP-bound Encounter state, the nucleotide-free Canonical state, and a putative intermediate bridging the two states, the Transition-to-Canonical state. These structures, along with simulations and functional data, provide high-resolution snapshots of a plausible G protein activation trajectory and support a stepwise conformational model for G protein activation. This activation cascade closely parallels mechanisms proposed for human GPCRs, suggesting a conserved GPCR signaling mechanism.

papers.abstract: Despite their significance, the genetic and molecular bases of neurodevelopmental disorders remain poorly understood. In this study, using human brain organoids and mouse models, we show that loss of NDE1, a gene closely associated with microcephaly, disrupts progenitor identity, prolongs mitosis, and alters regional patterning in the forebrain. NDE1 knockout leads to a caudal identity shift of neural progenitor cells in the organoids and mouse brains, coinciding with aberrant ERK signaling. Notably, downstream activation of the ERK pathway restored rostral PAX6 expression in human brain organoids. Parallel analyses of Nde1 knockout mice confirmed disrupted regional patterning of the forebrain. Together, our data establish NDE1 as a critical regulator of early human brain regionalization and elucidate molecular mechanisms underlying the structural abnormalities observed in NDE1-associated microcephaly.

papers.abstract: Piezoelectric surface acoustic wave devices can drive charge carriers in semiconductors through the acoustoelectric effect, generating direct currents with potential applications in sensing and biomedicine. However, current sources based on this mechanism that combine nanoampere-level precision, a wide dynamic range, and long-term operational stability have yet to be demonstrated. Here, we demonstrate an acoustically driven current source based on an InSb heterostructure integrated with a piezoelectric substrate. The output current is tunable from 1.22 nA to 25.46 μA by adjusting the input radio-frequency power, with a sensitivity down to the nanoampere scale. At an input power of 10 mW, the device delivers an average output current of 1.54 μA with 1% accuracy and maintains a standard deviation of 4.82 nA over 12 h of continuous operation. Its acoustic-to-electrical conversion efficiency can be further enhanced by implementing multiple interdigital transducer arrays and single-phase unidirectional transducer structures, enabling cooperative excitation and directional acoustic energy propagation. The device also supports wireless excitation and accelerates wound healing in a rat full-thickness skin defect model under low-intensity electrical stimulation. These results establish a wireless acoustoelectric platform for stable, tunable, and miniaturized current delivery, suggesting potential for biomedical applications.

papers.abstract: Immunotherapy has revolutionized the treatment landscape for many cancers, but fails to improve the outcomes of glioblastoma multiforme (GBM), in which low tumor antigen presentation restricts the recognition and eradication of cancerous cells by immunocytes. We here report an approach to in situ reprogramming hypoimmunogenic glioblastoma stem cells (GSCs) into type 1 conventional dendritic cell (cDC1)-like cells for presenting endogenous tumor antigens and priming sustained tumoricidal T-cell responses. Specifically, our cavity-injectable nucleobase-derived lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-hydrogel superstructure efficiently delivers transcription factors (PU.1, IRF8, BATF3) and the costimulatory molecule (TNFSF9) into GSCs to induce cDC1-like reprogramming. These cDC1-like cells potentiate GBM immunogenicity, elicit robust adaptive immunity and long-term antitumor memory, thereby inhibiting tumor growth and preventing postoperative GBM relapse in mice. Collectively, this work establishes in situ tumor cell reprogramming into licensed cDC1-like cells as a therapeutic paradigm for converting immunologically "cold" tumors into a self-vaccinating immune niche with broad translational potential for hypoimmunogenic malignancy treatment.

papers.abstract: As sharing the anatomical entrance to the larynx, swallowing plays not only an important role in food and water intake, but also a major role in defensive mechanism for preventing the risk of foreign matter aspiration. Besides water/acid, the mechanical stimulation of food or foreign matter could induce swallowing, yet the relevant sensory pathways remain poorly understood. Here, using male mice as a model, we clarify that vagal sensory neurons expressing Piezo2 responsibly transmit swallowing induced mechanical stimuli from the pharynx to tyrosine hydroxylase positive (TH + ) neurons in the nucleus of the solitary tract (NTS), then to ambiguus nucleus/rostral ventrolateral medulla (Amb/RVLM complex). Specific activation of Piezo2+ vagal sensory neurons or TH + NTS neurons can induce swallowing behavior. Either inhibition of TH + NTS neurons or Piezo2 knockout in vagal sensory neurons can abolish swallowing reflex. Notably, we elucidate that the TH + NTS-Amb/RVLM pathway serves as a shared downstream pathway for both mechanical and chemical stimuli-elicited swallowing. Collectively, we describe a pharynx-to-brain sensory pathway that provides a basis for central integration of swallowing and airway defensive reflexes.

papers.abstract: Our previous study revealed that Piezo1 in colonic goblet cells senses mechanical stimuli to regulate the production and secretion of MUC2, but the underlying mechanism remains unclear. Altered endoplasmic reticulum function and the unfolded protein response (UPR), which are critical for MUC2 protein folding and secretion, were observed in goblet cell-specific Piezo1 knockout mice. This study aimed to investigate whether and how Piezo1 in goblet cells modulates mucus barrier function by regulating the UPR. In vitro, LS174T cells were subjected to orbital shaking to simulate fluid shear stress (FSS) stimulation. The expression of UPR-related molecules and MUC2 was detected using real-time PCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence staining in the presence or absence of Piezo1 and UPR inhibition. In vivo, goblet cell-specific Piezo1 knockout (cKO) mice were treated with dextran sulphate sodium (DSS) and water avoidance stress (WAS). We analysed changes in goblet cell morphology, mucus layer thickness, UPR-related protein expression and ER structure. In addition, DSS-induced colitis mice were intraperitoneally injected with Yoda1 to activate Piezo1, and alterations in pathological structures and mucus layer thickness were subsequently evaluated. Compared with PERK or ATF6, FSS activated PIEZO1 and promoted calcium influx, thereby maintaining ER calcium homeostasis and selectively activating the IRE1α-XBP1 signalling pathway. This cascade facilitated MUC2 production, whereas pharmacological inhibition of PIEZO1 or IRE1α expression significantly abolished these effects. Compared with WT mice, cKO mice exhibited aggravated mucus barrier impairment, downregulated IRE1α-XBP1 and aggravated ER swelling under DSS and WAS. In contrast, pharmacological activation of Piezo1 via Yoda1 treatment restored intestinal mucus layer thickness and ameliorated colitis in DSS mice. Piezo1 senses mechanical stimulation to maintain ER calcium homeostasis and modulates the UPR via the IRE1α-XBP1 pathway, thereby facilitating MUC2 production in goblet cells and maintaining intestinal mucosal barrier homeostasis. Piezo1 in colonic goblet cells senses intestinal mechanical stimulation and modulates endoplasmic reticulum calcium homeostasis via Ca2+ influx. The Piezo1-Ca2+-IRE1α-XBP1 signaling axis controls Mucin2 synthesis and production to maintain intestinal mucus barrier integrity. Pharmacological activation of Piezo1 by Yoda1 rescues mucus barrier defects, providing a potential therapeutic strategy for gastrointestinal mucosal injury.

papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) is the leading cause of death among peritoneal dialysis (PD) patients, yet PD-specific biomarkers and prediction models remain limited. This study aimed to identify glycated peptide biomarkers associated with CVD in PD patients and develop a prediction model integrating glycated proteomics and clinical indicators using machine learning. In Phase I, a matched discovery cohort (48 PD patients with CVD and 48 without CVD) was used to identify glycated peptides by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), with glmnet used to prioritise candidate biomarkers. In Phase II, candidate biomarkers were quantified in a prospective internal derivation cohort (n = 240) and a multicentre external validation cohort (n = 102). The combined model was developed using F-test feature selection and elastic-net logistic regression. Its predictive performance was compared with three published cardiovascular risk models. Patients were stratified using a training-derived Youden cutoff. In the discovery cohort, 257 glycated peptides were differentially abundant between groups. Four candidate biomarkers were prioritised, and two peptides, GEAFTLK(g)ATVLNYLPK and K(g)QHLFVK, were retained in the final model together with six clinical indicators: phosphate, diabetes, total Kt/V, albumin, cardiac troponin T, and glycated albumin. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.784 in the training set, 0.781 in the internal testing set, and 0.822 in the external validation cohort, respectively. Using the training-derived cutoff of 0.373, higher 1-year CVD incidence was observed in the high-risk group in both validation cohorts. The combined model also achieved higher ROC-AUCs than the published cardiovascular risk models. We developed and externally validated a PD-specific CVD prediction model by integrating glycated peptide biomarkers with clinical indicators, which may facilitate earlier risk stratification and targeted prevention.

papers.abstract: Primary liver cancer, including hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (iCCA), remains a leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide. Therapeutic resistance substantially limits the efficacy of chemotherapy, targeted therapy, immunotherapy, and radiotherapy. For example, only approximately 30% of patients with HCC derive clinical benefit from sorafenib, and acquired resistance commonly develops within six months, underscoring the urgent need to clarify the molecular basis of treatment failure. Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed RNA molecules with high structural stability and tissue-specific expression. In liver cancer, circRNAs regulate therapeutic resistance through multiple mechanisms that converge on ferroptosis suppression, apoptosis evasion, DNA damage repair, oncogenic signaling, immune escape, and cancer stemness. Beyond the canonical competing endogenous RNA model, this review highlights emerging regulatory mechanisms involving RNA-binding protein interactions, circRNA-encoded functional micropeptides, and circRNA-mediated phase separation. Exosomal circRNAs also facilitate the intercellular transmission of resistant phenotypes and remodel the tumor immune microenvironment. We systematically summarize circRNA-mediated resistance across different therapeutic modalities and critically evaluate the available evidence according to experimental models, in vivo validation, and patient validation. Although circRNAs show potential as biomarkers for predicting therapeutic response and as targets for overcoming resistance, most candidates remain at the preclinical stage. Their clinical translation is constrained by the lack of standardized detection methods, insufficient multicenter validation, and inefficient and inadequately targeted in vivo delivery systems. Because most direct mechanistic evidence is derived from HCC, selected iCCA-related findings are incorporated where available.

papers.abstract: Interactions between T cell receptors (TCRs), peptides, and human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) underlie antigen-specific T cell immunity. Despite substantial advances in prediction methods, accurate modeling of coupled TCR-peptide-HLA recognition remains underdeveloped, limiting applications such as TCR and neoepitope prioritization in cancer and antigen identification in autoimmunity. Here we present StriMap, a unified framework for predicting TCR-peptide-HLA interactions by integrating physicochemical, sequence-context, and structural features at recognition interfaces. StriMap achieves state-of-the-art performance with improved generalizability and enables applications in cancer and autoimmunity. As a case study, we screened 13 million peptides from 43,241 bacterial proteins and identified candidate molecular mimics that were experimentally validated to activate T cells expressing an ankylosing spondylitis (AS)-associated TCR. A top validated peptide was enriched in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), suggesting potential shared microbial triggers. Overall, StriMap provides a framework for rational immunotherapy design and dissecting antigenic drivers of autoimmunity.

papers.abstract: Prostate intraepithelial neoplasia (PIN) is a recognized precursor to prostate cancer (PCa) and shares many histological and molecular features with invasive disease. To clarify the relationship between PIN and PCa, we performed integrated genomic and transcriptomic analyses on epithelial and stromal laser-capture microdissected samples in matched PIN (n = 121), PCa (n = 217), and adjacent normal (AN, n = 115) prostate tissue from formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples across three datasets. We identified two epithelial and two stromal transcriptomic clusters, termed 'invasive-like' and 'normal-like', which were present across all datasets. Among PIN samples, 46% of epithelial and 38% of stromal samples were classified as invasive-like. Whole-genome sequencing analysis revealed recurrent copy number alterations in PIN and PCa lesions, with recurrent copy number alterations more frequently shared between invasive-like PIN and PCa. This study provides new insight into PIN biology and the relationship between PIN and invasive PCa and highlights a transcriptional signature in PIN samples that may have prognostic implications. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: Measurable residual disease (MRD) has established itself as an essential post-treatment biomarker in chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL). While achieving undetectable MRD (uMRD) reliably predicts prolonged progression-free survival (PFS) for individual patients across clinical trials, establishing MRD as a universal, trial-level regulatory surrogate endpoint across contemporary targeted therapies remains a formidable biostatistical hurdle. This perspective addresses the "atomistic fallacy" underlying the apparent erosion of trial-level surrogacy observed in aggregate meta-analyses. We demonstrate that the attenuation of trial-level surrogacy stems from fundamental biological effect modification-specifically the distinction between cytostatic therapies (e.g., continuous Bruton tyrosine kinase inhibitors) and cytotoxic, deep-remission regimens (e.g., fixed-duration venetoclax combinations)-as well as operational confounders introduced by modern adaptive trial designs. Reconciling these individual- and trial-level observations requires transitioning from a binary endorsement model to a mechanism-dependent, context-specific framework for surrogate endpoint validation in CLL.

papers.abstract: Cancer therapies are commonly evaluated by target inhibition, pathway modulation, or initial tumor response, yet these measures do not reliably predict which treatments produce lasting disease control. Many pharmacodynamically active therapies produce transient benefit followed by relapse, while others achieve therapeutic durability despite comparable initial activity. This Perspective argues that durability is better explained by the behavior of the treated tumor system than by the depth of target suppression and distinguishes three modes of intervention behavior: buffered suppression, in which adaptive escape remains broadly accessible; adaptive constraint, in which future tumor states are narrowed without eradication; and collapse-dominant control, in which treatment drives a state transition that leaves few routes for persistence. Examples from targeted therapy, differentiation therapy, checkpoint blockade, and CAR-T therapy illustrate how the same modality can produce different intervention behaviors depending on tumor biology. A prospective sequence is also proposed for testing which behavior a candidate therapy is likely to induce.

papers.abstract: The revision of the WHO classification of CNS tumours now distinguishes grade 4 diffuse gliomas by their molecular features, but tailored treatment is yet to be standardised. Glioblastoma (isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH))-wildtype tumours harbouring an unmethylated O6-methylguanine-DNA methyltransferase "(uMGMT)" promoter are inherently resistant to temozolomide (TMZ). However, no standardised treatment recommendations are available for grade 4 astrocytoma IDH-mutant. We previously demonstrated that administration of bortezomib (BTZ) 48 h prior to TMZ depletes MGMT protein and sensitizes uMGMT glioma cells to TMZ. Based on these findings, a phase IB/II trial was initiated to evaluate the safety and clinical activity of sequential BTZ and TMZ. This interim analysis aimed to determine a futility safeguard, identify molecular and pharmacodynamic determinants of treatment response and failure in the first 15 patients consecutively treated. Adult patients with recurrent grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma or IDH-wildtype glioblastoma, uMGMT promoter, measurable disease, Karnofsky Performance Status ≥ 70, and disease progression ≥ 12 weeks after radiotherapy were enrolled. Patients received intravenous BTZ 1.3 mg/m² on days 1, 4, and 7 of each 28-day cycle, followed by oral TMZ 200 mg/m²/day for 5 consecutive days beginning on day 3. Targeted sequencing of glioma-associated genes and longitudinal plasma proteomic profiling using LC-MS/MS were performed before, during, and after treatment. Fifteen patients (median age 52 years) comprised 10 patients with IDH- wildtype glioblastoma and 5 patients with grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Disease control (partial response and stable disease) was observed in 4/10 (40%) IDH- wildtype glioblastoma patients, comprising one PR and three cases of SD. In contrast, all five patients with grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytoma experienced rapid progressive disease. Notably, non-responding IDH-wildtype glioblastomas and all IDH-mutant tumours harboured alterations affecting the CDKN2A/RB1-cell-cycle regulatory axis, including CDKN2A and/or RB1loss, with one IDH-mutant patient additionally harbouring PIK3CA gain. By comparison, responding IDH-wildtype glioblastomas were characterized by amplified EGFR, nuclear NF-κB (p65/RelA) activation, and absence of RB-pathway alterations. Longitudinal proteomic analyses demonstrated comparatively attenuated treatment-induced changes in proteins associated with invasion and extracellular matrix remodelling in responders, whereas proteins involved in damage clearance immune phenotype, platelet activation, aggregation, and degranulation were significantly altered during disease control. Sequential BTZ and TMZ therapy was feasible with manageable hematologic and non-hematologic toxicities and met prespecified interim futility criteria, supporting continued recruitment to the phase II study. Disease control was restricted to a molecularly defined subset of IDH- wildtype glioblastoma characterized by EGFR amplification and NF-κB activation. In contrast, universal treatment failure among grade 4 IDH-mutant astrocytomas was associated with alterations of the CDKN2A/RB1 cell-cycle checkpoint pathway, suggesting that advanced molecular evolution and cell-cycle deregulation may override the survival advantage typically associated with IDH-mutant gliomas and limit the effectiveness of MGMT-targeted sensitization strategies. papers.abstract: Acute allograft rejection is largely dependent on T cell-driven immune responses; however, the molecular programs that establish and maintain effector T cell states during rejection remain incompletely defined. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis was conducted to characterize the activation of signalling pathways in T cells during acute allograft rejection. The function of MEK1/2 signalling was evaluated both in vitro and in vivo using mice with targeted deletion of Mek1/2 in T cells and pharmacological inhibition. Phosphoproteomic analysis, immunofluorescence staining, and western blotting were conducted to investigate downstream signalling mechanisms, particularly those involving SMAD4. Effector CD4 and CD8 T cells exhibited enhanced MEK/ERK pathway activation throughout the rejection process. MEK1/2 inhibition, either via genetic deletion or pharmacological blockade, attenuated T cell activation and effector activity, leading to reduced rejection and prolonged graft survival. Phosphoproteomic analysis identified SMAD4 as a key downstream effector of MEK1/2 signalling. Mechanistically, MEK1/2 deficiency reduced SMAD4 nuclear translocation in activated T cells, accompanied by diminished effector T cell responses. MEK1/2 signalling regulates T cell activation and effector phenotypes via SMAD4 nuclear translocation in heart transplant rejection. Therapeutic intervention targeting this pathway may contribute to alloimmune response regulation and improve transplant outcomes.

papers.abstract: Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

papers.abstract: The photic environment is a key driver of fish ecology that shapes adaptations to aquatic habitats. The evolutionary history of these adaptations, however, is difficult to trace. Melanosomes, melanin-rich organelles, offer unique insights into physiology and ecology and often fossilise. Here, we present a comparative analysis of melanosomes from extant and fossil fishes to trace the evolution of ecological and physiological adaptations through deep time. Melanosomes from internal tissues of extant fishes exhibit highly conserved geometries in all major taxonomic groups examined, indicating persistent functional constraints during evolution. Larger, more abundant melanosomes in lungfish likely reflect adaptations that underpin the vertebrate water-to-land transition. In contrast, eye melanosomes exhibit lineage-specific patterns. Bony fishes possess cylindrical eye melanosomes associated with retinomotor movements, photoreceptor protection, and improved visual acuity, whereas jawless and cartilaginous fishes possess only spheroidal melanosomes, consistent with visual sensitivity and alternative light-regulation strategies including pupillary modulation. These taxonomic differences are preserved in fossils from the late Carboniferous Mazon Creek biota, indicating that links between melanosome morphology and function were established during the early evolutionary history of these lineages in the Ordovician, approximately 445 million years ago. Early innovations in melanin biology uniquely facilitated vertebrate sensory evolution and ecological diversification.

papers.abstract: Metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion are hallmarks of cancer metastasis, but how tumor metabolism shapes the immune microenvironment during colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains poorly understood. The role of E-cadherin (CDH1) beyond cell adhesion is unexplored. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime trajectory inference, and in vivo/in vitro functional assays in primary and liver-metastatic CRC models. CellChat was used to map intercellular communication. Histone lactylation, ADAM10 activation, and CDH1 shedding were validated by biochemical and immunohistochemical assays. PGK1-driven glycolysis is upregulated in liver metastases and promotes metastatic progression. Elevated lactate induces histone H3K18 lactylation, activating ADAM10 expression. ADAM10 cleaves CDH1, releasing its soluble ectodomain. This fragment acts as a ligand for KLRG1 on T cells, driving exhaustion and immunosuppression. Cell-cell communication analysis confirmed CDH1-KLRG1 as a top differentially activated pathway in metastasis. Functionally, targeting PGK1 or blocking CDH1 shedding inhibits liver metastasis and restores T-cell function. We identify a metabolic-epigenetic-immune axis in which tumor glycolysis reprograms immunity via lactate-induced CDH1 shedding. Soluble CDH1 functions as an immunomodulatory signal, linking metabolic activity to T-cell exhaustion. This redefines CDH1 as a dual-function molecule and reveals actionable targets for metastatic CRC. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

papers.abstract: The tumor-stroma percentage (TSP) has been proposed as a prognostic factor in ovarian cancer. When assessed manually by pathologists, the TSP can be subject to significant inter-rater variability. Automated methods for TSP determination have recently been developed. Existing approaches typically yield a single TSP value for a relatively small region of interest in the slide, introducing bias through region selection and potentially overlooking the TSP distribution across the entire histologically examined area. We present an adaptable deep learning pipeline, efficiently fine-tuned for ovarian cancer tissue analysis using a few-shot learning approach, requiring only minimal new training annotations. Instead of calculating a single TSP value, our method quantifies the global TSP distribution across the entire tumor and therefore captures its spatial heterogeneity. To identify a prognostic biomarker, we systematically evaluated a panel of metrics describing this distribution in 98 patients. Our analysis revealed that the mean-median difference of the TSP distribution [hazard ratio (HR) = 0.60, 95% CI = 0.46-0.79, p < 0.001], a quantitative measure of asymmetry, together with the mean TSP (HR = 0.65, 95% CI = 0.43-0.97, p = 0.03), are biomarkers significantly associated with recurrence-free survival. By successfully adapting a pipeline for ovarian cancer, we demonstrate that automated analysis of the entire TSP distribution provides significant prognostic information superior to that obtained by manual assessment. Spatial heterogeneity of the TSP is a key prognostic factor. © 2026 Fraunhofer IIS and The Author(s). papers.abstract: The aims of the study were to elucidate the regulatory role of rhomboid family protein 2 (RHBDF2) in breast cancer chemoresistance and the underlying molecular mechanisms to provide a theoretical basis and research direction to facilitate the development of potential therapeutic interventions. Chemoresistance and apoptosis assays, and mouse tumor-bearing models were used to evaluate the correlation between RHBDF2 expression and breast cancer chemoresistance. Doxorubicin accumulation, rhodamine efflux, immunohistochemical staining, Western blot, and quantitative polymerase chain reaction were used to validate the regulatory relationships in protein expression and function for RHBDF2, MDR1 (ABCB1), and SEC62 (a critical component of the endoplasmic reticulum membrane insertion machinery). Immunofluorescence staining and immunoprecipitation assays were employed to determine the molecular mechanisms underlying RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis-mediated regulation of breast cancer chemoresistance. The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis constitutes the core regulatory pathway in breast cancer chemoresistance. When RHBDF2 is highly expressed, it binds to heat shock cognate protein 70 (HSC70), a central chaperone-mediated autophagy receptor, thereby blocking the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62, maintaining SEC62 protein levels, and promoting membrane integration of MDR1 to enhance drug resistance. Under downregulated RHBDF2 expression, the HSC70-mediated degradation of SEC62 increases, leading to impaired MDR1 function and substantially reduced cellular drug resistance. The RHBDF2-SEC62-MDR1 axis is the core signaling pathway that governs chemoresistance in breast cancer. Targeted interventions against key molecules or related signaling nodes in this axis can provide a theoretical basis for developing novel therapeutic strategies to reverse chemoresistance, with great clinical translational value.

papers.abstract: Proficient mismatch repair colorectal cancer (pMMR-CRC) exhibits resistance to immunotherapy, presenting a significant clinical challenge that must be addressed. Exosomes, which serve as mediators of intercellular communication, play a crucial role in the tumor microenvironment (TME). However, the mechanisms that exosomes regulate tumor immunity in pMMR-CRC need to be fully elucidated. In this study, we discovered that circSENP5, a circular RNA (circRNA), is highly expressed in pMMR-CRC and is derived from exosomes that are transferred to tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs). This transfer enhances the oxidative phosphorylation of macrophages and promotes immunosuppressive characteristics, as well as increased levels of inhibitory receptors on CD8+ T cells. Mechanistically, circSENP5 binds to the deubiquitinase USP10, stabilizing LRPPRC, a key regulator of mitochondrial function. This interaction protects LRPPRC from ubiquitin-mediated degradation, resulting in enhanced mitochondrial respiration and immune suppression. in vivo, the overexpression of circSENP5 accelerates tumor progression, while its mutation disrupts the interaction with USP10, leading to reduced TAM infiltration and improved CD8+ T cell function. Targeting circSENP5 in combination with anti-PD-L1 immune checkpoint therapy effectively suppresses tumor progression, highlighting a potential therapeutic strategy. These findings suggest that exosomal circSENP5 plays a pivotal role in immune evasion in pMMR-CRC by modulating mitochondrial metabolism in TAMs, thereby providing potential therapeutic targets for overcoming immune resistance in pMMR-CRC.
